| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-orm_quarkus-hibernate-orm-flush-mode"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-orm.flush.mode`](#quarkus-hibernate-orm_quarkus-hibernate-orm-flush-mode) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-orm.flush.mode+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-orm."persistence-unit-name".flush.mode` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-orm."persistence-unit-name".flush.mode+++[]<br><br>The default flushing strategy, or when to flush entities to the database in a Hibernate session: before every query, on commit, ...<br><br>This default can be overridden on a per-session basis with `Session#setHibernateFlushMode()` or on a per-query basis with the hint `HibernateHints#HINT_FLUSH_MODE`.<br><br>See the javadoc of `org.hibernate.FlushMode` for details.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_ORM_FLUSH_MODE+++[] | tooltip:manual[The `org.hibernate.Session` is only flushed when `org.hibernate.Session#flush()` is called explicitly. This mode is very efficient for read-only transactions.], tooltip:commit[The `org.hibernate.Session` is flushed when `org.hibernate.Transaction#commit()` is called. It is never automatically flushed before query execution.], tooltip:auto[The `org.hibernate.Session` is flushed when `org.hibernate.Transaction#commit()` is called,opts=and is sometimes flushed before query execution in order to ensure that queries never return stale state. This is the default flush mode.], tooltip:always[The `org.hibernate.Session` is flushed when `org.hibernate.Transaction#commit()` is called and before every query. This is usually unnecessary and inefficient.] | tooltip:auto[The `org.hibernate.Session` is flushed when `org.hibernate.Transaction#commit()` is called,opts=and is sometimes flushed before query execution in order to ensure that queries never return stale state. This is the default flush mode.] |
| <mark>Hibernate Search Coordination with Outbox Polling</mark> | Type | Default |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-enabled"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.enabled`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-enabled) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.enabled+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.enabled` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.enabled+++[]<br><br>Whether the event processor is enabled, i.e. whether events will be processed to perform automatic reindexing on this instance of the application.<br><br>This can be set to `false` to disable event processing on some application nodes, for example to dedicate some nodes to HTTP request processing and other nodes to event processing.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_EVENT_PROCESSOR_ENABLED+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-shards-total-count"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.shards.total-count`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-shards-total-count) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.shards.total-count+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.shards.total-count` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.shards.total-count+++[]<br><br>The total number of shards that will form a partition of the entity change events to process.<br><br>By default, sharding is dynamic and setting this property is not necessary.<br><br>If you want to control explicitly the number and assignment of shards, you must configure static sharding and then setting this property as well as the assigned shards (see `shards.assigned`) is necessary.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor-sharding) for more information about event processor sharding.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_EVENT_PROCESSOR_SHARDS_TOTAL_COUNT+++[] | int |  |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-shards-assigned"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.shards.assigned`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-shards-assigned) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.shards.assigned+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.shards.assigned` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.shards.assigned+++[]<br><br>Among shards that will form a partition of the entity change events, the shards that will be processed by this application instance.<br><br>By default, sharding is dynamic and setting this property is not necessary.<br><br>If you want to control explicitly the number and assignment of shards, you must configure static sharding and then setting this property as well as the total shard count is necessary.<br><br>Shards are referred to by an index in the range `[0, total_count - 1]` (see `shards.total-count`). A given application node must be assigned at least one shard but may be assigned multiple shards by setting `shards.assigned` to a comma-separated list, e.g. `0,3`.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor-sharding) for more information about event processor sharding.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_EVENT_PROCESSOR_SHARDS_ASSIGNED+++[] | list of int |  |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-polling-interval"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.polling-interval`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-polling-interval) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.polling-interval+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.polling-interval` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.polling-interval+++[]<br><br>How long to wait for another query to the outbox events table after a query didn’t return any event.<br><br>Lower values will reduce the time it takes for a change to be reflected in the index, but will increase the stress on the database when there are no new events.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_EVENT_PROCESSOR_POLLING_INTERVAL+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `0.100S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-pulse-interval"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.pulse-interval`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-pulse-interval) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.pulse-interval+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.pulse-interval` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.pulse-interval+++[]<br><br>How long the event processor can poll for events before it must perform a "pulse", updating and checking registrations in the agents table.<br><br>The pulse interval must be set to a value between the polling interval and one third (1/3) of the expiration interval.<br><br>Low values (closer to the polling interval) mean less time wasted not processing events when a node joins or leaves the cluster, and reduced risk of wasting time not processing events because an event processor is incorrectly considered disconnected, but more stress on the database because of more frequent checks of the list of agents.<br><br>High values (closer to the expiration interval) mean more time wasted not processing events when a node joins or leaves the cluster, and increased risk of wasting time not processing events because an event processor is incorrectly considered disconnected, but less stress on the database because of less frequent checks of the list of agents.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_EVENT_PROCESSOR_PULSE_INTERVAL+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `2S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-pulse-expiration"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.pulse-expiration`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-pulse-expiration) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.pulse-expiration+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.pulse-expiration` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.pulse-expiration+++[]<br><br>How long an event processor "pulse" remains valid before considering the processor disconnected and forcibly removing it from the cluster.<br><br>The expiration interval must be set to a value at least 3 times larger than the pulse interval.<br><br>Low values (closer to the pulse interval) mean less time wasted not processing events when a node abruptly leaves the cluster due to a crash or network failure, but increased risk of wasting time not processing events because an event processor is incorrectly considered disconnected.<br><br>High values (much larger than the pulse interval) mean more time wasted not processing events when a node abruptly leaves the cluster due to a crash or network failure, but reduced risk of wasting time not processing events because an event processor is incorrectly considered disconnected.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_EVENT_PROCESSOR_PULSE_EXPIRATION+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `30S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-batch-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.batch-size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-batch-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.batch-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.batch-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.batch-size+++[]<br><br>How many outbox events, at most, are processed in a single transaction.<br><br>Higher values will reduce the number of transactions opened by the background process and may increase performance thanks to the first-level cache (persistence context), but will increase memory usage and in extreme cases may lead to ``OutOfMemoryError``s.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_EVENT_PROCESSOR_BATCH_SIZE+++[] | int | `50` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-transaction-timeout"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.transaction-timeout`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-transaction-timeout) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.transaction-timeout+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.transaction-timeout` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.transaction-timeout+++[]<br><br>The timeout for transactions processing outbox events.<br><br>When this property is not set, Hibernate Search will use whatever default transaction timeout is configured in the JTA transaction manager, which may be too low for batch processing and lead to transaction timeouts when processing batches of events. If this happens, set a higher transaction timeout for event processing using this property.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) |  |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-retry-delay"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.retry-delay`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-event-processor-retry-delay) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.event-processor.retry-delay+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.retry-delay` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.event-processor.retry-delay+++[]<br><br>How long the event processor must wait before re-processing an event after its previous processing failed.<br><br>Use the value `0S` to reprocess failed events as soon as possible, with no delay.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_EVENT_PROCESSOR_RETRY_DELAY+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `30S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-mass-indexer-polling-interval"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.mass-indexer.polling-interval`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-mass-indexer-polling-interval) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.mass-indexer.polling-interval+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.mass-indexer.polling-interval` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.mass-indexer.polling-interval+++[]<br><br>How long to wait for another query to the agent table when actively waiting for event processors to suspend themselves.<br><br>Low values will reduce the time it takes for the mass indexer agent to detect that event processors finally suspended themselves, but will increase the stress on the database while the mass indexer agent is actively waiting.<br><br>High values will increase the time it takes for the mass indexer agent to detect that event processors finally suspended themselves, but will reduce the stress on the database while the mass indexer agent is actively waiting.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-mass-indexer) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_MASS_INDEXER_POLLING_INTERVAL+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `0.100S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-mass-indexer-pulse-interval"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.mass-indexer.pulse-interval`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-mass-indexer-pulse-interval) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.mass-indexer.pulse-interval+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.mass-indexer.pulse-interval` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.mass-indexer.pulse-interval+++[]<br><br>How long the mass indexer can wait before it must perform a "pulse", updating and checking registrations in the agent table.<br><br>The pulse interval must be set to a value between the polling interval and one third (1/3) of the expiration interval.<br><br>Low values (closer to the polling interval) mean reduced risk of event processors starting to process events again during mass indexing because a mass indexer agent is incorrectly considered disconnected, but more stress on the database because of more frequent updates of the mass indexer agent's entry in the agent table.<br><br>High values (closer to the expiration interval) mean increased risk of event processors starting to process events again during mass indexing because a mass indexer agent is incorrectly considered disconnected, but less stress on the database because of less frequent updates of the mass indexer agent's entry in the agent table.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-mass-indexer) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_MASS_INDEXER_PULSE_INTERVAL+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `2S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-mass-indexer-pulse-expiration"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.mass-indexer.pulse-expiration`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-mass-indexer-pulse-expiration) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.mass-indexer.pulse-expiration+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.mass-indexer.pulse-expiration` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.mass-indexer.pulse-expiration+++[]<br><br>How long an event processor "pulse" remains valid before considering the processor disconnected and forcibly removing it from the cluster.<br><br>The expiration interval must be set to a value at least 3 times larger than the pulse interval.<br><br>Low values (closer to the pulse interval) mean less time wasted with event processors not processing events when a mass indexer agent terminates due to a crash, but increased risk of event processors starting to process events again during mass indexing because a mass indexer agent is incorrectly considered disconnected.<br><br>High values (much larger than the pulse interval) mean more time wasted with event processors not processing events when a mass indexer agent terminates due to a crash, but reduced risk of event processors starting to process events again during mass indexing because a mass indexer agent is incorrectly considered disconnected.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-mass-indexer) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_MASS_INDEXER_PULSE_EXPIRATION+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `30S` |

| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-enabled"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.enabled`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-enabled) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.enabled+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.enabled` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.enabled+++[]<br><br>Whether the event processor is enabled, i.e. whether events will be processed to perform automatic reindexing on this instance of the application.<br><br>This can be set to `false` to disable event processing on some application nodes, for example to dedicate some nodes to HTTP request processing and other nodes to event processing.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_TENANTS__TENANT_ID__EVENT_PROCESSOR_ENABLED+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-shards-total-count"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.shards.total-count`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-shards-total-count) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.shards.total-count+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.shards.total-count` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.shards.total-count+++[]<br><br>The total number of shards that will form a partition of the entity change events to process.<br><br>By default, sharding is dynamic and setting this property is not necessary.<br><br>If you want to control explicitly the number and assignment of shards, you must configure static sharding and then setting this property as well as the assigned shards (see `shards.assigned`) is necessary.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor-sharding) for more information about event processor sharding.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_TENANTS__TENANT_ID__EVENT_PROCESSOR_SHARDS_TOTAL_COUNT+++[] | int |  |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-shards-assigned"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.shards.assigned`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-shards-assigned) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.shards.assigned+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.shards.assigned` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.shards.assigned+++[]<br><br>Among shards that will form a partition of the entity change events, the shards that will be processed by this application instance.<br><br>By default, sharding is dynamic and setting this property is not necessary.<br><br>If you want to control explicitly the number and assignment of shards, you must configure static sharding and then setting this property as well as the total shard count is necessary.<br><br>Shards are referred to by an index in the range `[0, total_count - 1]` (see `shards.total-count`). | <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-batch-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.batch-size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-batch-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.batch-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.batch-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.batch-size+++[]<br><br>How many outbox events, at most, are processed in a single transaction.<br><br>Higher values will reduce the number of transactions opened by the background process and may increase performance thanks to the first-level cache (persistence context), but will increase memory usage and in extreme cases may lead to ``OutOfMemoryError``s.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_TENANTS__TENANT_ID__EVENT_PROCESSOR_BATCH_SIZE+++[] | int | `50` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-transaction-timeout"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.transaction-timeout`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-transaction-timeout) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.transaction-timeout+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.transaction-timeout` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.transaction-timeout+++[]<br><br>The timeout for transactions processing outbox events.<br><br>When this property is not set, Hibernate Search will use whatever default transaction timeout is configured in the JTA transaction manager, which may be too low for batch processing and lead to transaction timeouts when processing batches of events. If this happens, set a higher transaction timeout for event processing using this property.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_TENANTS__TENANT_ID__EVENT_PROCESSOR_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) |  |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-retry-delay"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.retry-delay`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-event-processor-retry-delay) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.retry-delay+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.retry-delay` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".event-processor.retry-delay+++[]<br><br>How long the event processor must wait before re-processing an event after its previous processing failed.<br><br>Use the value `0S` to reprocess failed events as soon as possible, with no delay.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-event-processor) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_TENANTS__TENANT_ID__EVENT_PROCESSOR_RETRY_DELAY+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `30S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-mass-indexer-polling-interval"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.polling-interval`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-mass-indexer-polling-interval) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.polling-interval+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.polling-interval` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.polling-interval+++[]<br><br>How long to wait for another query to the agent table when actively waiting for event processors to suspend themselves.<br><br>Low values will reduce the time it takes for the mass indexer agent to detect that event processors finally suspended themselves, but will increase the stress on the database while the mass indexer agent is actively waiting.<br><br>High values will increase the time it takes for the mass indexer agent to detect that event processors finally suspended themselves, but will reduce the stress on the database while the mass indexer agent is actively waiting.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-mass-indexer) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_TENANTS__TENANT_ID__MASS_INDEXER_POLLING_INTERVAL+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `0.100S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-mass-indexer-pulse-interval"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.pulse-interval`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-mass-indexer-pulse-interval) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.pulse-interval+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.pulse-interval` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.pulse-interval+++[]<br><br>How long the mass indexer can wait before it must perform a "pulse", updating and checking registrations in the agent table.<br><br>The pulse interval must be set to a value between the polling interval and one third (1/3) of the expiration interval.<br><br>Low values (closer to the polling interval) mean reduced risk of event processors starting to process events again during mass indexing because a mass indexer agent is incorrectly considered disconnected, but more stress on the database because of more frequent updates of the mass indexer agent's entry in the agent table.<br><br>High values (closer to the expiration interval) mean increased risk of event processors starting to process events again during mass indexing because a mass indexer agent is incorrectly considered disconnected, but less stress on the database because of less frequent updates of the mass indexer agent's entry in the agent table.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-mass-indexer) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_TENANTS__TENANT_ID__MASS_INDEXER_PULSE_INTERVAL+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `2S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-mass-indexer-pulse-expiration"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.pulse-expiration`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-outbox-polling_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-coordination-tenants-tenant-id-mass-indexer-pulse-expiration) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.pulse-expiration+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.pulse-expiration` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".coordination.tenants."tenant-id".mass-indexer.pulse-expiration+++[]<br><br>How long an event processor "pulse" remains valid before considering the processor disconnected and forcibly removing it from the cluster.<br><br>The expiration interval must be set to a value at least 3 times larger than the pulse interval.<br><br>Low values (closer to the pulse interval) mean less time wasted with event processors not processing events when a mass indexer agent terminates due to a crash, but increased risk of event processors starting to process events again during mass indexing because a mass indexer agent is incorrectly considered disconnected.<br><br>High values (much larger than the pulse interval) mean more time wasted with event processors not processing events when a mass indexer agent terminates due to a crash, but reduced risk of event processors starting to process events again during mass indexing because a mass indexer agent is incorrectly considered disconnected.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#coordination-outbox-polling-mass-indexer) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_COORDINATION_TENANTS__TENANT_ID__MASS_INDEXER_PULSE_EXPIRATION+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `30S` |

| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-active"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.active`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-active) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.active+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".active` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".active+++[]<br><br>Whether Hibernate Search should be active for this persistence unit at runtime.<br><br>If Hibernate Search is not active, it won't index Hibernate ORM entities, and accessing the SearchMapping/SearchSession of the relevant persistence unit for search or other operation will not be possible.<br><br>Note that if Hibernate Search is disabled (i.e. `quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.enabled` is set to `false`), it won't be active for any persistence unit, and setting this property to `true` will fail.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_ACTIVE+++[] | boolean | `'true' if Hibernate Search is enabled and the persistence unit is active; 'false' otherwise` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-schema-management-strategy"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.schema-management.strategy`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-schema-management-strategy) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.schema-management.strategy+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".schema-management.strategy` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".schema-management.strategy+++[]<br><br>The schema management strategy, controlling how indexes and their schema are created, updated, validated or dropped on startup and shutdown.<br><br>Available values:<br><br>!=== h!Strategy h!Definition<br><br>!none !Do nothing: assume that indexes already exist and that their schema matches Hibernate Search's expectations.<br><br>!validate !Validate that indexes exist and that their schema matches Hibernate Search's expectations.<br><br>If it does not, throw an exception, but make no attempt to fix the problem.<br><br>!create !For indexes that do not exist, create them along with their schema.<br><br>For indexes that already exist, do nothing: assume that their schema matches Hibernate Search's expectations.<br><br>!create-or-validate (**default** unless using Dev Services) !For indexes that do not exist, create them along with their schema.<br><br>For indexes that already exist, validate that their schema matches Hibernate Search's expectations.<br><br>If it does not, throw an exception, but make no attempt to fix the problem.<br><br>!create-or-update !For indexes that do not exist, create them along with their schema.<br><br>For indexes that already exist, validate that their schema matches Hibernate Search's expectations; if it does not match expectations, try to update it.<br><br>**This strategy is unfit for production environments**, due to several important limitations, but can be useful when developing.<br><br>!drop-and-create !For indexes that do not exist, create them along with their schema.<br><br>For indexes that already exist, drop them, then create them along with their schema.<br><br>!drop-and-create-and-drop (**default** when using Dev Services) !For indexes that do not exist, create them along with their schema.<br><br>For indexes that already exist, drop them, then create them along with their schema.<br><br>Also, drop indexes and their schema on shutdown. !===<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#mapper-orm-schema-management-strategy) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_SCHEMA_MANAGEMENT_STRATEGY+++[] | `none`, `validate`, `create`, `create-or-validate`, `create-or-update`, `drop-and-create`, `drop-and-create-and-drop` | `drop-and-create-and-drop when using Dev Services; create-or-validate otherwise` |

| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-indexing-plan-synchronization-strategy"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.indexing.plan.synchronization.strategy`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-indexing-plan-synchronization-strategy) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.indexing.plan.synchronization.strategy+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".indexing.plan.synchronization.strategy` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".indexing.plan.synchronization.strategy+++[]<br><br>How to synchronize between application threads and indexing, in particular when relying on (implicit) listener-triggered indexing on entity change, but also when using a `SearchIndexingPlan` explicitly.<br><br>Defines how complete indexing should be before resuming the application thread after a database transaction is committed.<br><br>> [!WARNING]<br>> Indexing synchronization is only relevant when coordination is disabled (which is the default).<br>><br>> With the [`outbox-polling` coordination strategy](/guides/hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch/index.md#coordination), indexing happens in background threads and is always asynchronous; the behavior is equivalent to the `write-sync` synchronization strategy.<br><br>Available values:<br><br>!=== .2+h!Strategy .2+h!Throughput 3+^h!Guarantees when the application thread resumes<br><br>h!Changes applied h!Changes safe from crash/power loss h!Changes visible on search<br><br>!async !Best ^![times] ^![times] ^![times]<br><br>!write-sync (**default**) !Medium ^![check] ^![check] ^![times]<br><br>!read-sync !Medium to worst ^![check] ^![times] ^![check]<br><br>!sync !Worst ^![check] ^![check] ^![check] !===<br><br>This property also accepts a [bean reference](/guides/hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch/index.md#bean-reference-note-anchor) to a custom implementations of `IndexingPlanSynchronizationStrategy`.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#indexing-plan-synchronization) for more information.<br><br>> [!NOTE]<br>> Instead of setting this configuration property, you can simply annotate your custom `IndexingPlanSynchronizationStrategy` implementation with `@SearchExtension` and leave the configuration property unset: Hibernate Search will use the annotated implementation automatically. See [this section](/guides/hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch/index.md#plugging-in-custom-components) for more information.<br>><br>> If this configuration property is set, it takes precedence over any `@SearchExtension` annotation.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_INDEXING_PLAN_SYNCHRONIZATION_STRATEGY+++[] | string | `write-sync` |

| [lock] <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-version"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.version`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-version) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.version+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".version` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".version+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.version` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.version+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".version` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".version+++[]<br><br>The version of Elasticsearch used in the cluster.<br><br>As the schema is generated without a connection to the server, this item is mandatory.<br><br>It doesn't have to be the exact version (it can be `7` or `7.1` for instance) but it has to be sufficiently precise to choose a model dialect (the one used to generate the schema) compatible with the protocol dialect (the one used to communicate with Elasticsearch).<br><br>There's no rule of thumb here as it depends on the schema incompatibilities introduced by Elasticsearch versions. | [lock] <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-schema-management-mapping-file"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.schema-management.mapping-file`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-schema-management-mapping-file) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.schema-management.mapping-file+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.mapping-file` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.mapping-file+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.schema-management.mapping-file` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.schema-management.mapping-file+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.mapping-file` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.mapping-file+++[]<br><br>Path to a file in the classpath holding a custom index mapping to be included in the index definition when creating an Elasticsearch index.<br><br>The file does not need to (and generally shouldn't) contain the full mapping: Hibernate Search will automatically inject missing properties (index fields) in the given mapping.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#backend-elasticsearch-mapping-custom) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_ELASTICSEARCH_SCHEMA_MANAGEMENT_MAPPING_FILE+++[] | string |  |

| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-thread-pool-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.thread-pool.size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-thread-pool-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.thread-pool.size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".thread-pool.size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".thread-pool.size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.thread-pool.size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.thread-pool.size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".thread-pool.size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".thread-pool.size+++[]<br><br>The size of the thread pool assigned to the backend.<br><br>Note that number is **per backend**, not per index. Adding more indexes will not add more threads.<br><br>As all operations happening in this thread-pool are non-blocking, raising its size above the number of processor cores available to the JVM will not bring noticeable performance benefit. The only reason to alter this setting would be to reduce the number of threads; for example, in an application with a single index with a single indexing queue, running on a machine with 64 processor cores, you might want to bring down the number of threads.<br><br>Defaults to the number of processor cores available to the JVM on startup.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_ELASTICSEARCH_THREAD_POOL_SIZE+++[] | int |  |

| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-schema-management-required-status-wait-timeout"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-schema-management-required-status-wait-timeout) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout+++[]<br><br>How long we should wait for the status before failing the bootstrap.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_ELASTICSEARCH_SCHEMA_MANAGEMENT_REQUIRED_STATUS_WAIT_TIMEOUT+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `10S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-indexing-queue-count"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.indexing.queue-count`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-indexing-queue-count) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.indexing.queue-count+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-count` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-count+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.indexing.queue-count` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.indexing.queue-count+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-count` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-count+++[]<br><br>The number of indexing queues assigned to each index.<br><br>Higher values will lead to more connections being used in parallel, which may lead to higher indexing throughput, but incurs a risk of overloading Elasticsearch, i.e. of overflowing its HTTP request buffers and tripping [circuit breakers](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.9/circuit-breaker.html), leading to Elasticsearch giving up on some request and resulting in indexing failures.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEXING_QUEUE_COUNT+++[] | int | `10` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-indexing-queue-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.indexing.queue-size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-indexing-queue-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.indexing.queue-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>The size of indexing queues.<br><br>Lower values may lead to lower memory usage, especially if there are many queues, but values that are too low will reduce the likeliness of reaching the max bulk size and increase the likeliness of application threads blocking because the queue is full, which may lead to lower indexing throughput.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEXING_QUEUE_SIZE+++[] | int | `1000` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-indexing-max-bulk-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.indexing.max-bulk-size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-indexing-max-bulk-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.indexing.max-bulk-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.max-bulk-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.max-bulk-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.indexing.max-bulk-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.indexing.max-bulk-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.max-bulk-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.max-bulk-size+++[]<br><br>The maximum size of bulk requests created when processing indexing queues.<br><br>Higher values will lead to more documents being sent in each HTTP request sent to Elasticsearch, which may lead to higher indexing throughput, but incurs a risk of overloading Elasticsearch, i.e. of overflowing its HTTP request buffers and tripping [circuit breakers](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.9/circuit-breaker.html), leading to Elasticsearch giving up on some request and resulting in indexing failures.<br><br>Note that raising this number above the queue size has no effect, as bulks cannot include more requests than are contained in the queue.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEXING_MAX_BULK_SIZE+++[] | int | `100` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-layout-strategy"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.layout.strategy`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-layout-strategy) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.layout.strategy+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".layout.strategy` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".layout.strategy+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.layout.strategy` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.layout.strategy+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".layout.strategy` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".layout.strategy+++[]<br><br>A [bean reference](/guides/hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch/index.md#bean-reference-note-anchor) to the component used to configure the Elasticsearch layout: index names, index aliases, ...<br><br>The referenced bean must implement `IndexLayoutStrategy`.<br><br>Available built-in implementations:<br><br>**`simple`**\<br>The default, future-proof strategy: if the index name in Hibernate Search is `myIndex`, this strategy will create an index named `myindex-000001`, an alias for write operations named `myindex-write`, and an alias for read operations named `myindex-read`.<br><br>**`no-alias`**\<br>A strategy without index aliases, mostly useful on legacy clusters: if the index name in Hibernate Search is `myIndex`, this strategy will create an index named `myindex`, and will not use any alias.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#backend-elasticsearch-indexlayout) for more information.<br><br>> [!NOTE]<br>> Instead of setting this configuration property, you can simply annotate your custom `IndexLayoutStrategy` implementation with `@SearchExtension` and leave the configuration property unset: Hibernate Search will use the annotated implementation automatically. See [this section](/guides/hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch/index.md#plugging-in-custom-components) for more information.<br>><br>> If this configuration property is set, it takes precedence over any `@SearchExtension` annotation.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_ELASTICSEARCH_LAYOUT_STRATEGY+++[] | string |  |

| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-indexes-index-name-indexing-queue-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch-indexes-index-name-indexing-queue-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch.indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch.indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-orm."persistence-unit-name".elasticsearch."backend-name".indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>The size of indexing queues.<br><br>Lower values may lead to lower memory usage, especially if there are many queues, but values that are too low will reduce the likeliness of reaching the max bulk size and increase the likeliness of application threads blocking because the queue is full, which may lead to lower indexing throughput.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_ORM_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEXES__INDEX_NAME__INDEXING_QUEUE_SIZE+++[] | int | `1000` |

See also link\:https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#mapping-reindexing-associationinverseside\\]`@AssociationInverseSide`\] link\:https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#mapping-reindexing-reindexonupdate\\]`@IndexingDependency(reindexOnUpdate = ...)`\].], tooltip:document[Entities indexed through Hibernate Search are the root of a document.  With this structure\: * An indexed entity "owns" other entities it references through associations,opts=which *cannot* be updated independently of the indexed entity; in particular they cannot be passed to {@link org.hibernate.search.mapper.pojo.standalone.work.SearchIndexingPlan#addOrUpdate(Object)}. * Therefore,when an entity changes,Hibernate Search doesn't need to resolve other entities to reindex,which means in particular that associations between entities can be uni-directional\: specifying the inverse side of associations through `@AssociationInverseSide` *is not required*.  See also link\:https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#mapping-reindexing-associationinverseside\\]`@AssociationInverseSide`\].] | tooltip:graph[Entities indexed through Hibernate Search are nodes in an entity graph.  With this structure\: * An indexed entity is independent of other entities it references through associations,opts=which *can* be updated independently of the indexed entity; in particular they may be passed to {@link org.hibernate.search.mapper.pojo.standalone.work.SearchIndexingPlan#addOrUpdate(Object)}. * Therefore,when an entity changes,Hibernate Search may need to resolve other entities to reindex,which means in particular that associations between entities must be bi-directional\: specifying the inverse side of associations through `@AssociationInverseSide` *is required*,unless reindexing is disabled for that association through `@IndexingDependency(reindexOnUpdate = ...)`.  See also link\:https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#mapping-reindexing-associationinverseside\\]`@AssociationInverseSide`\] link\:https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#mapping-reindexing-reindexonupdate\\]`@IndexingDependency(reindexOnUpdate = ...)`\].] |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-active"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.active`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-active) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.active+++[]<br><br>Whether Hibernate Search Standalone should be active at runtime.<br><br>If Hibernate Search Standalone is not active, it won't start with the application, and accessing the SearchMapping for search or other operations will not be possible.<br><br>Note that if Hibernate Search Standalone is disabled (i.e. `quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.enabled` is set to `false`), it won't be active, and setting this property to `true` will fail.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ACTIVE+++[] | boolean | `'true' if Hibernate Search Standalone is enabled; 'false' otherwise` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-schema-management-strategy"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.schema-management.strategy`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-schema-management-strategy) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.schema-management.strategy+++[]<br><br>The schema management strategy, controlling how indexes and their schema are created, updated, validated or dropped on startup and shutdown.<br><br>Available values:<br><br>!=== h!Strategy h!Definition<br><br>!none !Do nothing: assume that indexes already exist and that their schema matches Hibernate Search's expectations.<br><br>!validate !Validate that indexes exist and that their schema matches Hibernate Search's expectations.<br><br>If it does not, throw an exception, but make no attempt to fix the problem.<br><br>!create !For indexes that do not exist, create them along with their schema.<br><br>For indexes that already exist, do nothing: assume that their schema matches Hibernate Search's expectations.<br><br>!create-or-validate (**default** unless using Dev Services) !For indexes that do not exist, create them along with their schema.<br><br>For indexes that already exist, validate that their schema matches Hibernate Search's expectations.<br><br>If it does not, throw an exception, but make no attempt to fix the problem.<br><br>!create-or-update !For indexes that do not exist, create them along with their schema.<br><br>For indexes that already exist, validate that their schema matches Hibernate Search's expectations; if it does not match expectations, try to update it.<br><br>**This strategy is unfit for production environments**, due to several important limitations, but can be useful when developing.<br><br>!drop-and-create !For indexes that do not exist, create them along with their schema.<br><br>For indexes that already exist, drop them, then create them along with their schema.<br><br>!drop-and-create-and-drop (**default** when using Dev Services) !For indexes that do not exist, create them along with their schema.<br><br>For indexes that already exist, drop them, then create them along with their schema.<br><br>Also, drop indexes and their schema on shutdown. !===<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#schema-management-strategy) for more information.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_SCHEMA_MANAGEMENT_STRATEGY+++[] | `none`, `validate`, `create`, `create-or-validate`, `create-or-update`, `drop-and-create`, `drop-and-create-and-drop` | `drop-and-create-and-drop when using Dev Services; create-or-validate otherwise` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-indexing-plan-synchronization-strategy"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.indexing.plan.synchronization.strategy`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-indexing-plan-synchronization-strategy) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.indexing.plan.synchronization.strategy+++[]<br><br>How to synchronize between application threads and indexing, in particular when relying on (implicit) listener-triggered indexing on entity change, but also when using a `SearchIndexingPlan` explicitly.<br><br>Defines how complete indexing should be before resuming the application thread after a `SearchSession` is closed.<br><br>Available values:<br><br>!=== .2+h!Strategy .2+h!Throughput 3+^h!Guarantees when the application thread resumes<br><br>h!Changes applied h!Changes safe from crash/power loss h!Changes visible on search<br><br>!async !Best ^![times] ^![times] ^![times]<br><br>!write-sync (**default**) !Medium ^![check] ^![check] ^![times]<br><br>!read-sync !Medium to worst ^![check] ^![times] ^![check]<br><br>!sync !Worst ^![check] ^![check] ^![check] !===<br><br>This property also accepts a [bean reference](/guides/hibernate-search-orm-elasticsearch/index.md#bean-reference-note-anchor) to a custom implementations of `IndexingPlanSynchronizationStrategy`.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#indexing-plan-synchronization) for more information.<br><br>> [!NOTE]<br>> Instead of setting this configuration property, you can simply annotate your custom `IndexingPlanSynchronizationStrategy` implementation with `@SearchExtension` and leave the configuration property unset: Hibernate Search will use the annotated implementation automatically. If this configuration property is set, it takes precedence over any `@SearchExtension` annotation.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_INDEXING_PLAN_SYNCHRONIZATION_STRATEGY+++[] | string | `write-sync` |

| [lock] <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-version"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.version`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-version) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.version+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".version` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".version+++[]<br><br>The version of Elasticsearch used in the cluster.<br><br>As the schema is generated without a connection to the server, this item is mandatory.<br><br>It doesn't have to be the exact version (it can be `7` or `7.1` for instance) but it has to be sufficiently precise to choose a model dialect (the one used to generate the schema) compatible with the protocol dialect (the one used to communicate with Elasticsearch).<br><br>There's no rule of thumb here as it depends on the schema incompatibilities introduced by Elasticsearch versions. | <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-thread-pool-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.thread-pool.size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-thread-pool-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.thread-pool.size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".thread-pool.size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".thread-pool.size+++[]<br><br>The size of the thread pool assigned to the backend.<br><br>Note that number is **per backend**, not per index. Adding more indexes will not add more threads.<br><br>As all operations happening in this thread-pool are non-blocking, raising its size above the number of processor cores available to the JVM will not bring noticeable performance benefit. The only reason to alter this setting would be to reduce the number of threads; for example, in an application with a single index with a single indexing queue, running on a machine with 64 processor cores, you might want to bring down the number of threads.<br><br>Defaults to the number of processor cores available to the JVM on startup.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_THREAD_POOL_SIZE+++[] | int |  |
