| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-version-check-enabled"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.version-check.enabled`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-version-check-enabled) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.version-check.enabled+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".version-check.enabled` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".version-check.enabled+++[]<br><br>Whether Hibernate Search should check the version of the Elasticsearch cluster on startup.<br><br>Set to `false` if the Elasticsearch cluster may not be available on startup.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_VERSION_CHECK_ENABLED+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-schema-management-required-status"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.schema-management.required-status`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-schema-management-required-status) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.schema-management.required-status+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.required-status` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.required-status+++[]<br><br>The minimal [https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.17/cluster-health.html\[Elasticsearch](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.17/cluster-health.html[Elasticsearch) cluster status\] required on startup.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_SCHEMA_MANAGEMENT_REQUIRED_STATUS+++[] | `green`, `yellow`, `red` | `yellow` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-schema-management-required-status-wait-timeout"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-schema-management-required-status-wait-timeout) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".schema-management.required-status-wait-timeout+++[]<br><br>How long we should wait for the status before failing the bootstrap.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_SCHEMA_MANAGEMENT_REQUIRED_STATUS_WAIT_TIMEOUT+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `10S` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexing-queue-count"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexing.queue-count`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexing-queue-count) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexing.queue-count+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-count` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-count+++[]<br><br>The number of indexing queues assigned to each index.<br><br>Higher values will lead to more connections being used in parallel, which may lead to higher indexing throughput, but incurs a risk of overloading Elasticsearch, i.e. of overflowing its HTTP request buffers and tripping [circuit breakers](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.9/circuit-breaker.html), leading to Elasticsearch giving up on some request and resulting in indexing failures.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEXING_QUEUE_COUNT+++[] | int | `10` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexing-queue-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexing.queue-size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexing-queue-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>The size of indexing queues.<br><br>Lower values may lead to lower memory usage, especially if there are many queues, but values that are too low will reduce the likeliness of reaching the max bulk size and increase the likeliness of application threads blocking because the queue is full, which may lead to lower indexing throughput.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEXING_QUEUE_SIZE+++[] | int | `1000` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexing-max-bulk-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexing.max-bulk-size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexing-max-bulk-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexing.max-bulk-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.max-bulk-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexing.max-bulk-size+++[]<br><br>The maximum size of bulk requests created when processing indexing queues.<br><br>Higher values will lead to more documents being sent in each HTTP request sent to Elasticsearch, which may lead to higher indexing throughput, but incurs a risk of overloading Elasticsearch, i.e. of overflowing its HTTP request buffers and tripping [circuit breakers](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.9/circuit-breaker.html), leading to Elasticsearch giving up on some request and resulting in indexing failures.<br><br>Note that raising this number above the queue size has no effect, as bulks cannot include more requests than are contained in the queue.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEXING_MAX_BULK_SIZE+++[] | int | `100` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-layout-strategy"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.layout.strategy`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-layout-strategy) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.layout.strategy+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".layout.strategy` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".layout.strategy+++[]<br><br>A [bean reference](/guides/hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch/index.md#bean-reference-note-anchor) to the component used to configure the Elasticsearch layout: index names, index aliases, ...<br><br>The referenced bean must implement `IndexLayoutStrategy`.<br><br>Available built-in implementations:<br><br>**`simple`**\<br>The default, future-proof strategy: if the index name in Hibernate Search is `myIndex`, this strategy will create an index named `myindex-000001`, an alias for write operations named `myindex-write`, and an alias for read operations named `myindex-read`.<br><br>**`no-alias`**\<br>A strategy without index aliases, mostly useful on legacy clusters: if the index name in Hibernate Search is `myIndex`, this strategy will create an index named `myindex`, and will not use any alias.<br><br>See [this section of the reference documentation](https://docs.hibernate.org/search/8.4/reference/en-US/html_single/#backend-elasticsearch-indexlayout) for more information.<br><br>> [!NOTE]<br>> Instead of setting this configuration property, you can simply annotate your custom `IndexLayoutStrategy` implementation with `@SearchExtension` and leave the configuration property unset: Hibernate Search will use the annotated implementation automatically. See [this section](/guides/hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch/index.md#plugging-in-custom-components) for more information.<br>><br>> If this configuration property is set, it takes precedence over any `@SearchExtension` annotation.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_LAYOUT_STRATEGY+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_section_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexes"></a> [Per-index configuration overrides](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_section_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexes) | Type | Default |

| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexes-index-name-indexing-queue-count"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-count`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexes-index-name-indexing-queue-count) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-count+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-count` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-count+++[]<br><br>The number of indexing queues assigned to each index.<br><br>Higher values will lead to more connections being used in parallel, which may lead to higher indexing throughput, but incurs a risk of overloading Elasticsearch, i.e. of overflowing its HTTP request buffers and tripping [circuit breakers](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.9/circuit-breaker.html), leading to Elasticsearch giving up on some request and resulting in indexing failures.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEXES__INDEX_NAME__INDEXING_QUEUE_COUNT+++[] | int | `10` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexes-index-name-indexing-queue-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexes-index-name-indexing-queue-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexes."index-name".indexing.queue-size+++[]<br><br>The size of indexing queues.<br><br>Lower values may lead to lower memory usage, especially if there are many queues, but values that are too low will reduce the likeliness of reaching the max bulk size and increase the likeliness of application threads blocking because the queue is full, which may lead to lower indexing throughput.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEXES__INDEX_NAME__INDEXING_QUEUE_SIZE+++[] | int | `1000` |
| <a id="quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexes-index-name-indexing-max-bulk-size"></a> [`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexes."index-name".indexing.max-bulk-size`](#quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch_quarkus-hibernate-search-standalone-elasticsearch-indexes-index-name-indexing-max-bulk-size) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch.indexes."index-name".indexing.max-bulk-size+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexes."index-name".indexing.max-bulk-size` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.hibernate-search-standalone.elasticsearch."backend-name".indexes."index-name".indexing.max-bulk-size+++[]<br><br>The maximum size of bulk requests created when processing indexing queues.<br><br>Higher values will lead to more documents being sent in each HTTP request sent to Elasticsearch, which may lead to higher indexing throughput, but incurs a risk of overloading Elasticsearch, i.e. of overflowing its HTTP request buffers and tripping [circuit breakers](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.9/circuit-breaker.html), leading to Elasticsearch giving up on some request and resulting in indexing failures.<br><br>Note that raising this number above the queue size has no effect, as bulks cannot include more requests than are contained in the queue.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_HIBERNATE_SEARCH_STANDALONE_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEXES__INDEX_NAME__INDEXING_MAX_BULK_SIZE+++[] | int | `100` |

| [lock] <a id="quarkus-infinispan-client_quarkus-infinispan-client-devservices-shared"></a> [`quarkus.infinispan-client.devservices.shared`](#quarkus-infinispan-client_quarkus-infinispan-client-devservices-shared) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.infinispan-client.devservices.shared+++[]<br><br>Indicates if the Infinispan server managed by Quarkus Dev Services is shared. When shared, Quarkus looks for running containers using label-based service discovery. If a matching container is found, it is used, and so a second one is not started. Otherwise, Dev Services for Infinispan starts a new container.<br><br>The discovery uses the `quarkus-dev-service-infinispan` label. The value is configured using the `service-name` property.<br><br>Container sharing is only used in dev mode.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_INFINISPAN_CLIENT_DEVSERVICES_SHARED+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| [lock] <a id="quarkus-infinispan-client_quarkus-infinispan-client-devservices-service-name"></a> [`quarkus.infinispan-client.devservices.service-name`](#quarkus-infinispan-client_quarkus-infinispan-client-devservices-service-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.infinispan-client.devservices.service-name+++[]<br><br>The value of the `quarkus-dev-service-infinispan` label attached to the started container. This property is used when `shared` is set to `true`. In this case, before starting a container, Dev Services for Infinispan looks for a container with the `quarkus-dev-service-infinispan` label set to the configured value. If found, it will use this container instead of starting a new one. Otherwise, it starts a new container with the `quarkus-dev-service-infinispan` label set to the specified value.<br><br>This property is used when you need multiple shared Infinispan servers.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_INFINISPAN_CLIENT_DEVSERVICES_SERVICE_NAME+++[] | string | `infinispan` |

Note that only official Infinispan images are supported.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_INFINISPAN_CLIENT_DEVSERVICES_IMAGE_NAME+++[] | string | `quay.io/infinispan/server:latest` |

| [lock] <a id="quarkus-infinispan-client_quarkus-infinispan-client-devservices-site"></a> [`quarkus.infinispan-client.devservices.site`](#quarkus-infinispan-client_quarkus-infinispan-client-devservices-site) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.infinispan-client.devservices.site+++[]<br><br>Add a site name to start the Infinispan Server Container with Cross Site Replication enabled (ex. lon). Cross Site Replication is the capability to connect two separate Infinispan Server Clusters that might run in different Data Centers, and configure backup caches to copy the data across the clusters with active-active or active-passive replication. See more about Cross Site Replication in the Infinispan Documentation <https://infinispan.org/docs/stable/titles/xsite/xsite.html> Configure `mcast-port` to avoid forming a cluster with any other running Infinispan Server container.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_INFINISPAN_CLIENT_DEVSERVICES_SITE+++[] | string |  |

Set a different mcastPort to create a separate cluster in Docker (e. 46656). Available values: ++**++ `DIGEST-SHA-512` - Uses the SHA-512 hashing algorithm to securely hash and verify credentials. This is the default. ++**++ `DIGEST-MD5` - Uses the MD5 hashing algorithm in addition to nonces to encrypt credentials. ++**++ `EXTERNAL` - Uses client certificates to provide valid identities to Infinispan Server and enable encryption. ++**++ `PLAIN` - Sends credentials in plain text (unencrypted) over the wire in a way that is similar to HTTP BASIC authentication. You should use `PLAIN` authentication only in combination with TLS encryption.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_INFINISPAN_CLIENT__CLIENT_NAME__SASL_MECHANISM+++[] | string | `DIGEST-SHA-512` |

| [lock] <a id="quarkus-kubernetes-client_quarkus-kubernetes-client-devservices-shared"></a> [`quarkus.kubernetes-client.devservices.shared`](#quarkus-kubernetes-client_quarkus-kubernetes-client-devservices-shared) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.kubernetes-client.devservices.shared+++[]<br><br>Indicates if the Kubernetes cluster managed by Quarkus Dev Services is shared. When shared, Quarkus looks for running containers using label-based service discovery. If a matching container is found, it is used, and so a second one is not started. Otherwise, Dev Services for Kubernetes starts a new container.<br><br>The discovery uses the `quarkus-dev-service-kubernetes` label. This property is used when `shared` is set to `true`. In this case, before starting a container, Dev Services for Kubernetes looks for a container with the `quarkus-dev-service-kubernetes` label set to the configured value. If found, it will use this container instead of starting a new one. Otherwise, it starts a new container with the `quarkus-dev-service-kubernetes` label set to the specified value.<br><br>This property is used when you need multiple shared Kubernetes clusters.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_KUBERNETES_CLIENT_DEVSERVICES_SERVICE_NAME+++[] | string | `kubernetes` |

| <a id="quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-port"></a> [`quarkus.mailer.port`](#quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-port) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer.port+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".port` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".port+++[]<br><br>The SMTP port. The default value depends on the configuration. The port 25 is used as default when `ssl` is disabled. This port continues to be used primarily for SMTP relaying. SMTP relaying is the transmission of email from email server to email server. The port 587 is the default port when `ssl` is enabled. It ensures that email is submitted securely.<br><br>Note that the port 465 may be used by SMTP servers, however, IANA has reassigned a new service to this port, and it should no longer be used for SMTP communications.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MAILER_PORT+++[] | int |  |

| <a id="quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-password"></a> [`quarkus.mailer.password`](#quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-password) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer.password+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".password` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".password+++[]<br><br>Sets the password to connect to the SMTP server.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MAILER_PASSWORD+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-tls-configuration-name"></a> [`quarkus.mailer.tls-configuration-name`](#quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-tls-configuration-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer.tls-configuration-name+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".tls-configuration-name` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".tls-configuration-name+++[]<br><br>The name of the TLS configuration to use.<br><br>If a name is configured, it uses the configuration from `quarkus.tls.<name>.*` If a name is configured, but no TLS configuration is found with that name then an error will be thrown.<br><br>If no TLS configuration name is set then, the specific TLS configuration (from `quarkus.mailer.*`) will be used.<br><br>The default TLS configuration is **not** used by default.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MAILER_TLS_CONFIGURATION_NAME+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-tls"></a> [`quarkus.mailer.tls`](#quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-tls) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer.tls+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".tls` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".tls+++[]<br><br>Whether the connection should be secured using TLS.<br><br>SMTP allows establishing connection with or without TLS. When establishing a connection with TLS, the connection is secured and encrypted. When establishing a connection without TLS, it can be secured and encrypted later using the STARTTLS command. In this case, the connection is initially unsecured and unencrypted. To configure this case, set this property to `false` and `start-tls` to `REQUIRED` Note that if a TLS configuration is set, TLS is enabled automatically. So, setting this property to `false` is required to not establish a connection with TLS.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MAILER_TLS+++[] | boolean |  |

| <a id="quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-disable-esmtp"></a> [`quarkus.mailer.disable-esmtp`](#quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-disable-esmtp) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer.disable-esmtp+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".disable-esmtp` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".disable-esmtp+++[]<br><br>Disable ESMTP.<br><br>The RFC-1869 states that clients should always attempt `EHLO` as first command to determine if ESMTP is supported, if this returns an error code, `HELO` is tried to use the *regular* SMTP command.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MAILER_DISABLE_ESMTP+++[] | boolean | `false` |

| <a id="quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-truststore-type"></a> [`quarkus.mailer.truststore.type`](#quarkus-mailer_quarkus-mailer-truststore-type) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer.truststore.type+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".truststore.type` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mailer."mailer-name".truststore.type+++[]<br><br>Sets the trust store type. | <a id="quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-connection-string"></a> [`quarkus.mongodb.connection-string`](#quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-connection-string) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb.connection-string+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".connection-string` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".connection-string+++[]<br><br>Configures the connection string. The format is: `mongodb://[username:password@]host1[:port1][,host2[:port2],...[,hostN[:portN]]][/[database.collection][?options]]`<br><br>`mongodb://` is a required prefix to identify that this is a string in the standard connection format.<br><br>`username:password@` are optional. If given, the driver will attempt to log in to a database after connecting to a database server. For some authentication mechanisms, only the username is specified and the password is not, in which case the ":" after the username is left off as well.<br><br>`host1` is the only required part of the connection string. It identifies a server address to connect to.<br><br>`:portX` is optional and defaults to :27017 if not provided.<br><br>`/database` is the name of the database to log in to and thus is only relevant if the `username:password@` syntax is used. If not specified the `admin` database will be used by default.<br><br>`?options` are connection options. Note that if `database` is absent there is still a `/` required between the last host and the `?` introducing the options. Options are name=value pairs and the pairs are separated by "&".<br><br>An alternative format, using the `mongodb{plus}srv` protocol, is:<br><br>```<br>mongodb+srv://[username:password@]host[/[database][?options]]<br>```<br><br>\* `mongodb{plus}srv://` is a required prefix for this format. \* `username:password@` are optional. If given, the driver will attempt to login to a database after connecting to a database server. For some authentication mechanisms, only the username is specified and the password is not, in which case the ":" after the username is left off as well \* `host` is the only required part of the URI. It identifies a single host name for which SRV records are looked up from a Domain Name Server after prefixing the host name with `"_mongodb._tcp"`. The host/port for each SRV record becomes the seed list used to connect, as if each one were provided as host/port pair in a URI using the normal mongodb protocol. \* `/database` is the name of the database to login to and thus is only relevant if the `username:password@` syntax is used. If not specified the "admin" database will be used by default. \* `?options` are connection options. Note that if `database` is absent there is still a `/` required between the last host and the `?` introducing the options. Options are name=value pairs and the pairs are separated by "&". Additionally with the mongodb{plus}srv protocol, TXT records are looked up from a Domain Name Server for the given host, and the text value of each one is prepended to any options on the URI itself. Because the last specified value for any option wins, that means that options provided on the URI will override any that are provided via TXT records.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING+++[] | string |  |

The addresses are passed as `host:port`.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_HOSTS+++[] | list of string | `127.0.0.1:27017` |

| [lock] <a id="quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-devservices-shared"></a> [`quarkus.mongodb.devservices.shared`](#quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-devservices-shared) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb.devservices.shared+++[]<br><br>Indicates if the MongoDB server managed by Quarkus Dev Services is shared. When shared, Quarkus looks for running containers using label-based service discovery. If a matching container is found, it is used, and so a second one is not started. Otherwise, Dev Services for MongoDB starts a new container.<br><br>The discovery uses the `quarkus-dev-service-mongodb` label. The value is configured using the `service-name` property.<br><br>Container sharing is only used in dev mode.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_DEVSERVICES_SHARED+++[] | boolean | `true` |

This property is used when `shared` is set to `true`. In this case, before starting a container, Dev Services for MongoDB looks for a container with the `quarkus-dev-service-mongodb` label set to the configured value. If found, it will use this container instead of starting a new one. Otherwise it starts a new container with the `quarkus-dev-service-mongodb` label set to the specified value.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_DEVSERVICES_SERVICE_NAME+++[] | string | `mongodb` |

| <a id="quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-write-concern-safe"></a> [`quarkus.mongodb.write-concern.safe`](#quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-write-concern-safe) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb.write-concern.safe+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".write-concern.safe` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".write-concern.safe+++[]<br><br>Configures the safety. If set to `true`: the driver ensures that all writes are acknowledged by the MongoDB server, or else throws an exception. (see also `w` and `wtimeoutMS`). If set fo `false`: the driver does not ensure that all writes are acknowledged by the MongoDB server.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_WRITE_CONCERN_SAFE+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-write-concern-journal"></a> [`quarkus.mongodb.write-concern.journal`](#quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-write-concern-journal) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb.write-concern.journal+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".write-concern.journal` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".write-concern.journal+++[]<br><br>Configures the journal writing aspect. If set to `true`: the driver waits for the server to group commit to the journal file on disk. If set to `false`: the driver does not wait for the server to group commit to the journal file on disk.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_WRITE_CONCERN_JOURNAL+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-write-concern-w"></a> [`quarkus.mongodb.write-concern.w`](#quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-write-concern-w) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb.write-concern.w+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".write-concern.w` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".write-concern.w+++[]<br><br>When set, the driver adds `w: wValue` to all write commands. It requires `safe` to be `true`. The value is typically a number, but can also be the `majority` string.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_WRITE_CONCERN_W+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-write-concern-retry-writes"></a> [`quarkus.mongodb.write-concern.retry-writes`](#quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-write-concern-retry-writes) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb.write-concern.retry-writes+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".write-concern.retry-writes` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".write-concern.retry-writes+++[]<br><br>If set to `true`, the driver will retry supported write operations if they fail due to a network error.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_WRITE_CONCERN_RETRY_WRITES+++[] | boolean | `false` |

| <a id="quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-credentials-auth-mechanism"></a> [`quarkus.mongodb.credentials.auth-mechanism`](#quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-credentials-auth-mechanism) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb.credentials.auth-mechanism+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".credentials.auth-mechanism` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".credentials.auth-mechanism+++[]<br><br>Configures the authentication mechanism to use if a credential was supplied. For the GSSAPI and MONGODB-X509 mechanisms, no password is accepted, only the username. Supported values: null or `GSSAPI\|PLAIN\|MONGODB-X509\|SCRAM_SHA_1\|SCRAM_SHA_256\|MONGODB_AWS`<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_CREDENTIALS_AUTH_MECHANISM+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-credentials-auth-source"></a> [`quarkus.mongodb.credentials.auth-source`](#quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-credentials-auth-source) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb.credentials.auth-source+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".credentials.auth-source` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb."mongo-client-name".credentials.auth-source+++[]<br><br>Configures the source of the authentication credentials. This is typically the database where the credentials have been created. This option is only respected when using the MONGO-CR mechanism (the default).<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_CREDENTIALS_AUTH_SOURCE+++[] | string |  |

| <a id="quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-tracing-command-detail-level"></a> [`quarkus.mongodb.tracing.command-detail-level`](#quarkus-mongodb-client_quarkus-mongodb-tracing-command-detail-level) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.mongodb.tracing.command-detail-level+++[]<br><br>Defines what information from MongoDB commands is included in traces.<br><br>\* **OFF** (default): No command information is included (only operation name, database, collection) \* **SANITIZED**: Command structure with BSON type information instead of actual values \* **FULL**: Complete command with all data (NOT recommended for production - may expose sensitive data)<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_MONGODB_TRACING_COMMAND_DETAIL_LEVEL+++[] | tooltip:off[No command details,opts=only operation metadata], tooltip:sanitized[Command structure with type information (e.g.,opts=++{++"email"\: "<string>",age,\: "<int32>"++}++)], tooltip:full[Full command including all data - may expose sensitive information] | tooltip:off[No command details,opts=only operation metadata] |

| <a id="quarkus-narayana-jta_quarkus-transaction-manager-reaper-check-period"></a> [`quarkus.transaction-manager.reaper.check-period`](#quarkus-narayana-jta_quarkus-transaction-manager-reaper-check-period) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.transaction-manager.reaper.check-period+++[]<br><br>The interval at which the reaper checks for timed-out transactions.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TRANSACTION_MANAGER_REAPER_CHECK_PERIOD+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `120S` |
| <a id="quarkus-narayana-jta_quarkus-transaction-manager-reaper-cancel-wait-period"></a> [`quarkus.transaction-manager.reaper.cancel-wait-period`](#quarkus-narayana-jta_quarkus-transaction-manager-reaper-cancel-wait-period) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.transaction-manager.reaper.cancel-wait-period+++[]<br><br>The time the reaper waits before interrupting a cancel worker that is rolling back a timed-out transaction.<br><br>When a transaction exceeds its timeout, the reaper schedules a cancel and waits this period before interrupting the cancel worker. In CPU-constrained environments (e.g., containers with strict CPU limits), the default of 500ms may be too aggressive, causing premature zombie transaction declarations.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TRANSACTION_MANAGER_REAPER_CANCEL_WAIT_PERIOD+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `500MS` |
| <a id="quarkus-narayana-jta_quarkus-transaction-manager-reaper-cancel-fail-wait-period"></a> [`quarkus.transaction-manager.reaper.cancel-fail-wait-period`](#quarkus-narayana-jta_quarkus-transaction-manager-reaper-cancel-fail-wait-period) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.transaction-manager.reaper.cancel-fail-wait-period+++[]<br><br>The time the reaper waits after interrupting a cancel worker before declaring the transaction a zombie.<br><br>After interrupting a cancel worker, the reaper waits this period. If the worker has not completed by then, the transaction is marked as a zombie. In CPU-constrained environments, increasing this value gives the application thread more time to respond to the cancellation.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TRANSACTION_MANAGER_REAPER_CANCEL_FAIL_WAIT_PERIOD+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `500MS` |
| <a id="quarkus-narayana-jta_quarkus-transaction-manager-reaper-zombie-max"></a> [`quarkus.transaction-manager.reaper.zombie-max`](#quarkus-narayana-jta_quarkus-transaction-manager-reaper-zombie-max) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.transaction-manager.reaper.zombie-max+++[]<br><br>The maximum number of zombie transactions before the reaper escalates to ERROR-level logging.<br><br>A zombie transaction is one where the cancel worker was unable to roll it back within the configured wait periods. Once this threshold is reached, subsequent zombies are logged at ERROR level instead of WARN.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TRANSACTION_MANAGER_REAPER_ZOMBIE_MAX+++[] | int | `8` |

If the value is not absolute then the directory is relative to the *user.dir* system property.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TRANSACTION_MANAGER_OBJECT_STORE_DIRECTORY+++[] | string | `ObjectStore` |

Either use XA for all resources if you want consistency, or split the code into separate methods with separate transactions.<br><br>Note that using a single XA unaware resource together with XA aware resources, known as the Last Resource Commit Optimization (LRCO), is different from using multiple XA unaware resources. Although LRCO allows most transactions to complete normally, some errors can cause an inconsistent transaction outcome. Using multiple XA unaware resources is not recommended since the probability of inconsistent outcomes is significantly higher and much harder to recover from than LRCO. For this reason, use LRCO as a last resort.<br><br>We do not recommend using this configuration property, and we plan to remove it in the future, so you should plan fixing your application accordingly. | <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-issuer"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.issuer`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-issuer) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.issuer+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.issuer` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.issuer+++[]<br><br>The expected issuer `iss` claim value. This property overrides the `issuer` property, which might be set in OpenId Connect provider's well-known configuration. If the `iss` claim value varies depending on the host, IP address, or tenant id of the provider, you can skip the issuer verification by setting this property to `any`, but it should be done only when other options (such as configuring the provider to use the fixed `iss` claim value) are not possible.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_ISSUER+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-audience"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.audience`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-audience) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.audience+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.audience` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.audience+++[]<br><br>The expected audience `aud` claim value, which can be a string or an array of strings. Note the audience claim is verified for ID tokens by default. ID token audience must be equal to the value of `quarkus.oidc.client-id` property. Use this property to override the expected value if your OpenID Connect provider sets a different audience claim value in ID tokens. Set it to `any` if your provider does not set ID token audience\` claim. Audience verification for access tokens is only done if this property is configured.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_AUDIENCE+++[] | list of string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-subject-required"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.subject-required`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-subject-required) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.subject-required+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.subject-required` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.subject-required+++[]<br><br>Require that the token includes a `sub` (subject) claim which is a unique and never reassigned identifier for the current user. Note that if you enable this property and if UserInfo is also required, both the token and UserInfo `sub` claims must be present and match each other.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_SUBJECT_REQUIRED+++[] | boolean | `false` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-required-claims-claim-name"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.required-claims."claim-name"`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-required-claims-claim-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.required-claims."claim-name"+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.required-claims."claim-name"` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.required-claims."claim-name"+++[]<br><br>A map of required claims and their expected values. For example, `quarkus.oidc.token.required-claims.org_id = org_xyz` would require tokens to have the `org_id` claim to be present and set to `org_xyz`. On the other hand, if it was set to `org_xyz,org_abc`, the `org_id` claim would need to have both `org_xyz` and `org_abc` values. Strings and arrays of strings are currently the only supported types. Use `SecurityIdentityAugmentor` to verify claims of other types or complex claims.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_REQUIRED_CLAIMS__CLAIM_NAME_+++[] | Map\<String,Set\<String>> |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-token-type"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.token-type`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-token-type) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.token-type+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.token-type` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.token-type+++[]<br><br>Expected token type<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_TOKEN_TYPE+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-lifespan-grace"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.lifespan-grace`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-lifespan-grace) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.lifespan-grace+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.lifespan-grace` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.lifespan-grace+++[]<br><br>Life span grace period in seconds. When checking token expiry, current time is allowed to be later than token expiration time by at most the configured number of seconds. When checking token issuance, current time is allowed to be sooner than token issue time by at most the configured number of seconds.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_LIFESPAN_GRACE+++[] | int |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-age"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.age`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-age) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.age+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.age` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.age+++[]<br><br>Token age. It allows for the number of seconds to be specified that must not elapse since the `iat` (issued at) time. A small leeway to account for clock skew which can be configured with `quarkus.oidc.token.lifespan-grace` to verify the token expiry time can also be used to verify the token age property. Note that setting this property does not relax the requirement that Bearer and Code Flow JWT tokens must have a valid (`exp`) expiry claim value. The only exception where setting this property relaxes the requirement is when a logout token is sent with a back-channel logout request since the current OpenId Connect Back-Channel specification does not explicitly require the logout tokens to contain an `exp` claim. However, even if the current logout token is allowed to have no `exp` claim, the `exp` claim is still verified if the logout token contains it.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_AGE+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-issued-at-required"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.issued-at-required`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-issued-at-required) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.issued-at-required+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.issued-at-required` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.issued-at-required+++[]<br><br>Require that the token includes a `iat` (issued at) claim Set this property to `false` if your JWT token does not contain an `iat` (issued at) claim. Note that ID token is always required to have an `iat` claim and therefore this property has no impact on the ID token verification process.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_ISSUED_AT_REQUIRED+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-principal-claim"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.principal-claim`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-principal-claim) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.principal-claim+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.principal-claim` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.principal-claim+++[]<br><br>Name of the claim which contains a principal name. By default, the `upn`, `preferred_username` and `sub` claims are checked.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_PRINCIPAL_CLAIM+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-refresh-expired"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.refresh-expired`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-refresh-expired) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.refresh-expired+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.refresh-expired` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.refresh-expired+++[]<br><br>Refresh expired authorization code flow ID or access tokens. If this property is enabled, a refresh token request is performed if the authorization code ID or access token has expired and, if successful, the local session is updated with the new set of tokens. Otherwise, the local session is invalidated and the user redirected to the OpenID Provider to re-authenticate. In this case, the user might not be challenged again if the OIDC provider session is still active. For this option be effective the `authentication.session-age-extension` property should also be set to a nonzero value since the refresh token is currently kept in the user session. This option is valid only when the application is of type `ApplicationType#WEB_APP`. This property is enabled if `quarkus.oidc.token.refresh-token-time-skew` is configured, you do not need to enable this property manually in this case.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_REFRESH_EXPIRED+++[] | boolean | `false` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-refresh-token-time-skew"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.refresh-token-time-skew`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-refresh-token-time-skew) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.refresh-token-time-skew+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.refresh-token-time-skew` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.refresh-token-time-skew+++[]<br><br>The refresh token time skew, in seconds. If this property is enabled, the configured number of seconds is added to the current time when checking if the authorization code ID or access token should be refreshed. If the sum is greater than the authorization code ID or access token's expiration time, a refresh is going to happen.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_REFRESH_TOKEN_TIME_SKEW+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-refresh-token-cache-time-to-live"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.refresh-token-cache-time-to-live`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-refresh-token-cache-time-to-live) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.refresh-token-cache-time-to-live+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.refresh-token-cache-time-to-live` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.refresh-token-cache-time-to-live+++[]<br><br>Duration for which a completed token refresh result is kept in memory.<br><br>When multiple concurrent requests carry the same expired session, each independently attempts to refresh the token. If the OIDC provider restricts how many times a refresh token can be used, duplicate refresh attempts may be rejected. Set this property to a short duration (for example, 5 seconds) to ensure only one refresh call is made and subsequent requests reuse the cached result.<br><br>Keep the value short (a few seconds) — it only needs to cover the window between concurrent requests arriving at the server. The cached tokens begin aging immediately, so longer values serve increasingly stale tokens without benefit.<br><br>The cache is per application instance with up to 10,000 entries.<br><br>This property is only effective when `refresh-expired()` is enabled.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_REFRESH_TOKEN_CACHE_TIME_TO_LIVE+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `0S` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-forced-jwk-refresh-interval"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.forced-jwk-refresh-interval`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-forced-jwk-refresh-interval) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.forced-jwk-refresh-interval+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.forced-jwk-refresh-interval` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.forced-jwk-refresh-interval+++[]<br><br>The forced JWK set refresh interval in minutes.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_FORCED_JWK_REFRESH_INTERVAL+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `10M` |

| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-decrypt-id-token"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token.decrypt-id-token`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-decrypt-id-token) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token.decrypt-id-token+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.decrypt-id-token` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token.decrypt-id-token+++[]<br><br>Decrypt ID token. Otherwise, if the JWT authentication token key is available, then it will be used to decrypt the token. Finally, if a client secret is configured, it will be used as a secret key to decrypt the token.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_DECRYPT_ACCESS_TOKEN+++[] | boolean | `false` |

| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-redirect-path"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.redirect-path`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-redirect-path) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.redirect-path+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.redirect-path` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.redirect-path+++[]<br><br>The relative path for calculating a `redirect_uri` query parameter. It has to start from a forward slash and is appended to the request URI's host and port. For example, if the current request URI is `https://localhost:8080/service`, a `redirect_uri` parameter is set to `https://localhost:8080/` if this property is set to `/` and be the same as the request URI if this property has not been configured. Note the original request URI is restored after the user has authenticated if `restorePathAfterRedirect` is set to `true`.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_REDIRECT_PATH+++[] | string |  |

Note if `redirectPath` property is not set, the original request URI is restored even if this property is disabled.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_RESTORE_PATH_AFTER_REDIRECT+++[] | boolean | `false` |

| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-error-path"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.error-path`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-error-path) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.error-path+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.error-path` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.error-path+++[]<br><br>Relative path to the public endpoint which processes the error response from the OIDC authorization endpoint. If the user authentication has failed, the OIDC provider returns an `error` and an optional `error_description` parameters, instead of the expected authorization `code`. If this property is set, the user is redirected to the endpoint which can return a user-friendly error description page. It has to start from a forward slash and is appended to the request URI's host and port. For example, if it is set as `/error` and the current request URI is `https://localhost:8080/callback?error=invalid_scope`, a redirect is made to `https://localhost:8080/error?error=invalid_scope`. If this property is not set, HTTP 401 status is returned in case of the user authentication failure.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_ERROR_PATH+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-session-expired-path"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.session-expired-path`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-session-expired-path) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.session-expired-path+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.session-expired-path` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.session-expired-path+++[]<br><br>Relative path to the public endpoint which an authenticated user is redirected to when the session has expired.<br><br>When the OIDC session has expired and the session can not be refreshed, a user is redirected to the OIDC provider to re-authenticate. The user experience may not be ideal in this case as it may not be obvious to the authenticated user why an authentication challenge is returned.<br><br>Set this property if you would like the user whose session has expired be redirected to a public application specific page instead, which can inform that the session has expired and advise the user to re-authenticated by following a link to the secured initial entry page.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_SESSION_EXPIRED_PATH+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-verify-access-token"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.verify-access-token`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-verify-access-token) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.verify-access-token+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.verify-access-token` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.verify-access-token+++[]<br><br>Both ID and access tokens are fetched from the OIDC provider as part of the authorization code flow.<br><br>ID token is always verified on every user request as the primary token which is used to represent the principal and extract the roles.<br><br>Authorization code flow access token is meant to be propagated to downstream services and is not verified by default unless `quarkus.oidc.roles.source` property is set to `accesstoken` which means the authorization decision is based on the roles extracted from the access token.<br><br>Authorization code flow access token verification is also enabled if this token is injected as JsonWebToken. Set this property to `false` if it is not required.<br><br>Bearer access token is always verified.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_VERIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN+++[] | boolean | `true when access token is injected as the JsonWebToken bean, false otherwise` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-force-redirect-https-scheme"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.force-redirect-https-scheme`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-force-redirect-https-scheme) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.force-redirect-https-scheme+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.force-redirect-https-scheme` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.force-redirect-https-scheme+++[]<br><br>Force `https` as the `redirect_uri` parameter scheme when running behind an SSL/TLS terminating reverse proxy. This property, if enabled, also affects the logout `post_logout_redirect_uri` and the local redirect requests.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_FORCE_REDIRECT_HTTPS_SCHEME+++[] | boolean | `false` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-scopes"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.scopes`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-scopes) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.scopes+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.scopes` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.scopes+++[]<br><br>List of scopes<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_SCOPES+++[] | list of string |  |

A single space is used by default.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_SCOPE_SEPARATOR+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-nonce-required"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.nonce-required`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-nonce-required) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.nonce-required+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.nonce-required` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.nonce-required+++[]<br><br>Require that ID token includes a `nonce` claim which must match `nonce` authentication request query parameter. | <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-add-openid-scope"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.add-openid-scope`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-add-openid-scope) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.add-openid-scope+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.add-openid-scope` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.add-openid-scope+++[]<br><br>Add the `openid` scope automatically to the list of scopes. | <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-forward-params"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.forward-params`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-forward-params) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.forward-params+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.forward-params` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.forward-params+++[]<br><br>Request URL query parameters which, if present, are added to the authentication redirect URI.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_FORWARD_PARAMS+++[] | list of string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-cookie-force-secure"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.cookie-force-secure`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-cookie-force-secure) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.cookie-force-secure+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.cookie-force-secure` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.cookie-force-secure+++[]<br><br>If enabled the state, session, and post logout cookies have their `secure` parameter set to `true` when HTTP is used. For example, a session cookie name for the default OIDC tenant is `q_session` but can be changed to `q_session_test` if this property is set to `test`.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_COOKIE_SUFFIX+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-cookie-path"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.cookie-path`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-cookie-path) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.cookie-path+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.cookie-path` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.cookie-path+++[]<br><br>Cookie path parameter value which, if set, is used to set a path parameter for the session, state and post logout cookies. The `cookie-path-header` property, if set, is checked first.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_COOKIE_PATH+++[] | string | `/` |

| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-cookie-domain"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.cookie-domain`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-cookie-domain) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.cookie-domain+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.cookie-domain` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.cookie-domain+++[]<br><br>Cookie domain parameter value which, if set, is used for the session, state and post logout cookies.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_COOKIE_DOMAIN+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-cookie-same-site"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.cookie-same-site`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-cookie-same-site) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.cookie-same-site+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.cookie-same-site` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.cookie-same-site+++[]<br><br>SameSite attribute for the session cookie.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_COOKIE_SAME_SITE+++[] | `strict`, `lax`, `none` | `lax` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-state-cookie-same-site"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.state-cookie-same-site`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-state-cookie-same-site) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.state-cookie-same-site+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.state-cookie-same-site` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.state-cookie-same-site+++[]<br><br>SameSite attribute for the state cookie.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_STATE_COOKIE_SAME_SITE+++[] | `strict`, `lax`, `none` | `lax` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-allow-multiple-code-flows"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.allow-multiple-code-flows`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-allow-multiple-code-flows) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.allow-multiple-code-flows+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.allow-multiple-code-flows` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.allow-multiple-code-flows+++[]<br><br>If a state cookie is present, a `state` query parameter must also be present and both the state cookie name suffix and state cookie value must match the value of the `state` query parameter when the redirect path matches the current path. However, if multiple authentications are attempted from the same browser, for example, from the different browser tabs, then the currently available state cookie might represent the authentication flow initiated from another tab and not related to the current request. Disable this property to permit only a single authorization code flow in the same browser.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_ALLOW_MULTIPLE_CODE_FLOWS+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-fail-on-missing-state-param"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.fail-on-missing-state-param`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-fail-on-missing-state-param) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.fail-on-missing-state-param+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.fail-on-missing-state-param` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.fail-on-missing-state-param+++[]<br><br>Fail with the HTTP 401 error if the state cookie is present but no state query parameter is present.<br><br>When either multiple authentications are disabled or the redirect URL matches the original request URL, the stale state cookie might remain in the browser cache from the earlier failed redirect to an OpenId Connect provider and be visible during the current request. For example, if Single-page application (SPA) uses XHR to handle redirects to the provider which does not support CORS for its authorization endpoint, the browser blocks it and the state cookie created by Quarkus remains in the browser cache. Quarkus reports an authentication failure when it detects such an old state cookie but find no matching state query parameter.<br><br>Reporting HTTP 401 error is usually the right thing to do in such cases, it minimizes a risk of the browser redirect loop but also can identify problems in the way SPA or Quarkus application manage redirects. For example, enabling `java-script-auto-redirect` or having the provider redirect to URL configured with `redirect-path` might be needed to avoid such errors.<br><br>However, setting this property to `false` might help if the above options are not suitable. It causes a new authentication redirect to OpenId Connect provider. Doing so might increase the risk of browser redirect loops.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_FAIL_ON_MISSING_STATE_PARAM+++[] | boolean | `false` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-fail-on-unresolved-kid"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.fail-on-unresolved-kid`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-fail-on-unresolved-kid) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.fail-on-unresolved-kid+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.fail-on-unresolved-kid` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.fail-on-unresolved-kid+++[]<br><br>Fail with the HTTP 401 error if the ID token signature can not be verified during the re-authentication only due to an unresolved token key identifier (`kid`).<br><br>This property might need to be disabled when multiple tab authentications are allowed, with one of the tabs keeping an expired ID token with its `kid` unresolved due to the verification key set refreshed due to another tab initiating an authorization code flow. In such cases, instead of failing with the HTTP 401 error, redirecting the user to re-authenticate with the HTTP 302 status may provide better user experience.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_FAIL_ON_UNRESOLVED_KID+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-user-info-required"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.user-info-required`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-user-info-required) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.user-info-required+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.user-info-required` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.user-info-required+++[]<br><br>If this property is set to `true`, an OIDC UserInfo endpoint is called.<br><br>This property is enabled automatically if `quarkus.oidc.roles.source` is set to `userinfo` or `quarkus.oidc.token.verify-access-token-with-user-info` is set to `true` or `quarkus.oidc.authentication.id-token-required` is set to `false`, the current OIDC tenant must support a UserInfo endpoint in these cases.<br><br>It is also enabled automatically if `io.quarkus.oidc.UserInfo` injection point is detected but only if the current OIDC tenant supports a UserInfo endpoint.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_USER_INFO_REQUIRED+++[] | boolean | `true when UserInfo bean is injected, false otherwise` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-session-age-extension"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.session-age-extension`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-session-age-extension) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.session-age-extension+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.session-age-extension` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.session-age-extension+++[]<br><br>Session age extension in minutes. The user session age property is set to the value of the ID token life-span by default and the user is redirected to the OIDC provider to re-authenticate once the session has expired. If this property is set to a nonzero value, then the expired ID token can be refreshed before the session has expired. This property is effective only if the `token.refresh-expired` property is enabled and a refresh token is available. It is set to 5 minutes by default.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_SESSION_AGE_EXTENSION+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `5M` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-state-cookie-age"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.state-cookie-age`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-state-cookie-age) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.state-cookie-age+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.state-cookie-age` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.state-cookie-age+++[]<br><br>State cookie age in minutes. State cookie is created every time a new authorization code flow redirect starts and removed when this flow is completed. State cookie name is unique by default, see `allow-multiple-code-flows`. Keep its age to the reasonable minimum value such as 5 minutes or less.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_STATE_COOKIE_AGE+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `5M` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-java-script-auto-redirect"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.java-script-auto-redirect`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-java-script-auto-redirect) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.java-script-auto-redirect+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.java-script-auto-redirect` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.java-script-auto-redirect+++[]<br><br>If this property is set to `true`, a normal 302 redirect response is returned if the request was initiated by a JavaScript API such as XMLHttpRequest or Fetch and the current user needs to be (re)authenticated, which might not be desirable for Single-page applications (SPA) since it automatically following the redirect might not work given that OIDC authorization endpoints typically do not support CORS.<br><br>If this property is set to `false`, a status code of `499` is returned to allow SPA to handle the redirect manually if a request header identifying current request as a JavaScript request is found. `X-Requested-With` request header with its value set to either `JavaScript` or `XMLHttpRequest` is expected by default if this property is enabled. You can register a custom `JavaScriptRequestChecker` to do a custom JavaScript request check instead.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_JAVA_SCRIPT_AUTO_REDIRECT+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-id-token-required"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.id-token-required`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-id-token-required) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.id-token-required+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.id-token-required` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.id-token-required+++[]<br><br>Requires that ID token is available when the authorization code flow completes. Disable this property only when you need to use the authorization code flow with OAuth2 providers which do not return ID token - an internal IdToken is generated in such cases.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_ID_TOKEN_REQUIRED+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-internal-id-token-lifespan"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.internal-id-token-lifespan`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-internal-id-token-lifespan) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.internal-id-token-lifespan+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.internal-id-token-lifespan` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.internal-id-token-lifespan+++[]<br><br>Internal ID token lifespan. This property is only checked when an internal IdToken is generated when OAuth2 providers do not return IdToken. If this property is not configured then an access token `expires_in` property in the OAuth2 authorization code flow response is used to set an internal IdToken lifespan.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_INTERNAL_ID_TOKEN_LIFESPAN+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-pkce-required"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.pkce-required`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-pkce-required) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.pkce-required+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.pkce-required` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.pkce-required+++[]<br><br>Requires that a Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) is used.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_PKCE_REQUIRED+++[] | boolean | `false` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-state-secret"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.state-secret`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-state-secret) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.state-secret+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.state-secret` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.state-secret+++[]<br><br>Secret used to encrypt Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) code verifier and/or nonce in the code flow state. This secret should be at least 32 characters long.<br><br>If this secret is not set, the client secret configured with either `quarkus.oidc.credentials.secret` or `quarkus.oidc.credentials.client-secret.value` is checked. Finally, `quarkus.oidc.credentials.jwt.secret` which can be used for `client_jwt_secret` authentication is checked. A client secret is not be used as a state encryption secret if it is less than 32 characters long.  The secret is auto-generated if it remains uninitialized after checking all of these properties.<br><br>Error is reported if the secret length is less than 16 characters.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_STATE_SECRET+++[] | string |  |

| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-par-enabled"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.authentication.par.enabled`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-authentication-par-enabled) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.authentication.par.enabled+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.par.enabled` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".authentication.par.enabled+++[]<br><br>If the pushed authorization request is enabled for this OIDC tenant.
