Default TokenStateManager encrypts a session cookie that keeps the tokens. Custom TokenStateManager do not have to encrypt tokens, they will already be encrypted by the time it is asked to store tokens.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_STATE_MANAGER_ENCRYPTION_REQUIRED+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-state-manager-encryption-secret"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token-state-manager.encryption-secret`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-state-manager-encryption-secret) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token-state-manager.encryption-secret+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token-state-manager.encryption-secret` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token-state-manager.encryption-secret+++[]<br><br>The secret used by the TokenStateManager to encrypt the session cookie storing the tokens when `encryption-required` property is enabled.<br><br>If this secret is not set, the client secret configured with either `quarkus.oidc.credentials.secret` or `quarkus.oidc.credentials.client-secret.value` is checked. Finally, `quarkus.oidc.credentials.jwt.secret` which can be used for `client_jwt_secret` authentication is checked. The secret is auto-generated every time an application starts if it remains uninitialized after checking all of these properties. Generated secret can not decrypt the session cookie or token encrypted before the restart, therefore a user re-authentication will be required.<br><br>The length of the secret used to encrypt the tokens should be at least 32 characters long. A warning is logged if the secret length is less than 16 characters.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_STATE_MANAGER_ENCRYPTION_SECRET+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-state-manager-encryption-algorithm"></a> [`quarkus.oidc.token-state-manager.encryption-algorithm`](#quarkus-oidc_quarkus-oidc-token-state-manager-encryption-algorithm) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc.token-state-manager.encryption-algorithm+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc."tenant".token-state-manager.encryption-algorithm` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc."tenant".token-state-manager.encryption-algorithm+++[]<br><br>Session cookie or token key encryption algorithm<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_STATE_MANAGER_ENCRYPTION_ALGORITHM+++[] | tooltip:a256-gcmkw[Content encryption key will be generated and encrypted using the A256GCMKW algorithm and the configured encryption secret. The generated content encryption key will be used to encrypt the session cookie content.], tooltip:dir[The configured key encryption secret will be used as the content encryption key to encrypt the session cookie content. Using the direct encryption avoids a content encryption key generation step and will make the encrypted session cookie sequence slightly shorter.  Avoid using the direct encryption if the encryption secret is less than 32 characters long.] | tooltip:a256-gcmkw[Content encryption key will be generated and encrypted using the A256GCMKW algorithm and the configured encryption secret. The generated content encryption key will be used to encrypt the session cookie content.] |

| <a id="quarkus-oidc-client_quarkus-oidc-client-connection-delay"></a> [`quarkus.oidc-client.connection-delay`](#quarkus-oidc-client_quarkus-oidc-client-connection-delay) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc-client.connection-delay+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc-client."id".connection-delay` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc-client."id".connection-delay+++[]<br><br>The duration to attempt the initial connection to an OIDC server. | <a id="quarkus-oidc-client_quarkus-oidc-client-connection-retry-count"></a> [`quarkus.oidc-client.connection-retry-count`](#quarkus-oidc-client_quarkus-oidc-client-connection-retry-count) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc-client.connection-retry-count+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc-client."id".connection-retry-count` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc-client."id".connection-retry-count+++[]<br><br>The number of times to retry re-establishing an existing OIDC connection if it is temporarily lost. | <a id="quarkus-oidc-client_quarkus-oidc-client-grant-type"></a> [`quarkus.oidc-client.grant.type`](#quarkus-oidc-client_quarkus-oidc-client-grant-type) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc-client.grant.type+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.oidc-client."id".grant.type` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.oidc-client."id".grant.type+++[]<br><br>Grant type<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OIDC_CLIENT_GRANT_TYPE+++[] | tooltip:client['client_credentials' grant requiring an OIDC client authentication only], tooltip:password['password' grant requiring both OIDC client and user ('username' and 'password') authentications], tooltip:code['authorization_code' grant requiring an OIDC client authentication as well as at least 'code' and 'redirect_uri' parameters which must be passed to OidcClient at the token request time.], tooltip:exchange['urn\:ietf\:params\:oauth\:grant-type\:token-exchange' grant requiring an OIDC client authentication as well as at least 'subject_token' parameter which must be passed to OidcClient at the token request time.], tooltip:jwt['urn\:ietf\:params\:oauth\:grant-type\:jwt-bearer' grant requiring an OIDC client authentication as well as at least an 'assertion' parameter which must be passed to OidcClient at the token request time.], tooltip:refresh['refresh_token' grant requiring an OIDC client authentication and a refresh token. Note,opts=OidcClient supports this grant by default if an access token acquisition response contained a refresh token. However,in some cases,the refresh token is provided out of band,for example,it can be shared between several of the confidential client's services,etc. If 'quarkus.oidc-client.grant-type' is set to 'refresh' then `OidcClient` will only support refreshing the tokens.], tooltip:ciba['urn\:openid\:params\:grant-type\:ciba' grant requiring an OIDC client authentication as well as 'auth_req_id' parameter which must be passed to OidcClient at the token request time.], tooltip:device['urn\:ietf\:params\:oauth\:grant-type\:device_code' grant requiring an OIDC client authentication as well as 'device_code' parameter which must be passed to OidcClient at the token request time.], tooltip:preauthorized-code['urn\:ietf\:params\:oauth\:grant-type\:pre-authorized_code' grant requiring an OIDC client authentication as well as at least a 'pre-authorized_code' parameter which must be passed to OidcClient at the token request time.] | tooltip:client['client_credentials' grant requiring an OIDC client authentication only] |

If unset, defaults to `OtlpExporterRuntimeConfig#DEFAULT_GRPC_BASE_URI`.<br><br>There is a generic property, that will apply to all signals and a signal specific one, following the pattern: `quarkus.otel.exporter.otlp..endpoint` where  is one of the supported signal types, like `traces` or `metrics`.<br><br>If protocol is `http/protobuf` the version and signal will be appended to the path (e.g. v1/traces or v1/metrics) and the default port will be `OtlpExporterRuntimeConfig#DEFAULT_HTTP_BASE_URI`.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT+++[] | string | `http://localhost:4317/` |

The format is similar to the `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` environment variable, a list of key-value pairs separated by the "=" character. i.e.: key1=value1,key2=value2<br><br>There is a generic property, that will apply to all signals and a signal specific one, following the pattern: `quarkus.otel.exporter.otlp..headers` where  is one of the supported signal types, like `traces` or `metrics`.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS+++[] | list of string |  |

Currently supported compression methods include `gzip` and `none`.<br><br>There is a generic property, that will apply to all signals and a signal specific one, following the pattern: `quarkus.otel.exporter.otlp..compression` where  is one of the supported signal types, like `traces` or `metrics`.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_COMPRESSION+++[] | `gzip`, `none` |  |
| <a id="quarkus-opentelemetry_quarkus-otel-exporter-otlp-timeout"></a> [`quarkus.otel.exporter.otlp.timeout`](#quarkus-opentelemetry_quarkus-otel-exporter-otlp-timeout) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.otel.exporter.otlp.timeout+++[]<br><br>Sets the maximum time to wait for the collector to process an exported batch of telemetry data. | [lock] <a id="quarkus-quartz_quarkus-quartz-serialize-job-data"></a> [`quarkus.quartz.serialize-job-data`](#quarkus-quartz_quarkus-quartz-serialize-job-data) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.quartz.serialize-job-data+++[]<br><br>Instructs JDBCJobStore to serialize JobDataMaps in the BLOB column.<br><br>Ignored if using a `ram` store i.e `StoreType#RAM`.<br><br>If this is set to `true`, the JDBCJobStore will store the JobDataMaps in their serialize form in the BLOB Column. This is useful when you want to store complex JobData objects other than String. This is equivalent of setting `org.quartz.jobStore.useProperties` to `false`. **NOTE: When this option is set to `true`, all the non-String classes used in JobDataMaps have to be registered for serialization when building a native image**<br><br>If this is set to `false` (the default), the values can be stored as name-value pairs rather than storing more complex objects in their serialized form in the BLOB column. This can be handy, as you avoid the class versioning issues that can arise from serializing your non-String classes into a BLOB. This is equivalent of setting `org.quartz.jobStore.useProperties` to `true`.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_QUARTZ_SERIALIZE_JOB_DATA+++[] | boolean | `false` |

When not set, defaults to RESP 3. When protocol negotiation is disabled, this setting has no effect.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_PREFERRED_PROTOCOL_VERSION+++[] | `resp2`, `resp3` | `resp3` |
| <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-topology-cache-ttl"></a> [`quarkus.redis.topology-cache-ttl`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-topology-cache-ttl) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.topology-cache-ttl+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".topology-cache-ttl` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".topology-cache-ttl+++[]<br><br>The TTL of the topology cache. A topology cache is used by a clustered Redis client and a sentinel Redis client to prevent constantly sending topology discovery commands (`CLUSTER SLOTS` or `SENTINEL ...`).<br><br>This setting is only meaningful in case of a clustered Redis client and a sentinel Redis client and has no effect otherwise.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_TOPOLOGY_CACHE_TTL+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `1S` |
| <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-auto-failover"></a> [`quarkus.redis.auto-failover`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-auto-failover) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.auto-failover+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".auto-failover` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".auto-failover+++[]<br><br>Whether automatic failover is enabled. This only makes sense for sentinel clients with role of `MASTER` and is ignored otherwise.<br><br>If enabled, the sentinel client will additionally create a connection to one sentinel node and watch for failover events. When new master is elected, all connections to the old master are automatically closed and new connections to the new master are created. Automatic failover makes sense for connections executing regular commands, but not for connections used to subscribe to Redis pub/sub channels.<br><br>Note that there is a brief period of time between the old master failing and the new master being elected when the existing connections will temporarily fail all operations. After the new master is elected, the connections will automatically fail over and start working again.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_AUTO_FAILOVER+++[] | boolean | `false` |
| <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-topology"></a> [`quarkus.redis.topology`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-topology) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.topology+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".topology` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".topology+++[]<br><br>How the Redis topology is obtained. By default, the topology is discovered automatically. This is the only mode for the clustered and sentinel client. For replication client, topology may be set *statically*.<br><br>In case of a static topology for replication Redis client, the first node in the list is considered a *master* and the remaining nodes in the list are considered *replicas*.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_TOPOLOGY+++[] | `discover`, `static` | `discover` |
| <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-cluster-transactions"></a> [`quarkus.redis.cluster-transactions`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-cluster-transactions) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.cluster-transactions+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".cluster-transactions` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".cluster-transactions+++[]<br><br>How transactions are handled in a cluster. This only makes sense for cluster clients and is ignored otherwise.<br><br>By default, transactions in cluster are disabled and transaction commands fail.<br><br>When set to `single-node`, Redis transactions are supported in the cluster, but only when they target a single node. The `MULTI` command is queued and is only issued when the next command is executed. This next command binds the connection to the corresponding node of the Redis cluster (so it should have keys, otherwise the target node is random). All subsequent commands are targeted to that node. If some of the subsequent commands have a key that belongs to another node, the command will fail on the server side. If `WATCH` is used before `MULTI`, its key(s) determine to which node the connection is bound and the subsequent `MULTI` is not queued. If `WATCH` keys belong to multiple nodes, the command fails on the client side.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_CLUSTER_TRANSACTIONS+++[] | `disabled`, `single-node` | `disabled` |
| <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-client-name"></a> [`quarkus.redis.client-name`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-client-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.client-name+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".client-name` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".client-name+++[]<br><br>The client name used to identify the connection.<br><br>If the `RedisClientConfig#configureClientName()` is enabled, and this property is not set it will attempt to extract the value from the `RedisClientName#value()` annotation.<br><br>If the `RedisClientConfig#configureClientName()` is enabled, both this property and the `RedisClientName#value()` must adhere to the pattern '++\[++a-zA-Z0-9++ \\++-\_.\~++\]\*++'; if not, this may result in an incorrect client name after URI encoding.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_CLIENT_NAME+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-configure-client-name"></a> [`quarkus.redis.configure-client-name`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-configure-client-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.configure-client-name+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".configure-client-name` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".configure-client-name+++[]<br><br>Whether it should set the client name while connecting with Redis.<br><br>This is necessary because Redis only accepts `client=my-client-name` query parameter in version 6{plus}.<br><br>This property can be used with `RedisClientConfig#clientName()` configuration.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_CONFIGURE_CLIENT_NAME+++[] | boolean | `false` |
| <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-tls-configuration-name"></a> [`quarkus.redis.tls-configuration-name`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-tls-configuration-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.tls-configuration-name+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".tls-configuration-name` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".tls-configuration-name+++[]<br><br>The name of the TLS configuration to use.<br><br>If a name is configured, it uses the configuration from `quarkus.tls.<name>.*` If a name is configured, but no TLS configuration is found with that name then an error will be thrown.<br><br>If no TLS configuration name is set then, `quarkus.redis.$client-name.tls` will be used.<br><br>The default TLS configuration is **not** used by default.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_TLS_CONFIGURATION_NAME+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-hash-slot-cache-ttl"></a> <mark>link:#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-hash-slot-cache-ttl\[`quarkus.redis.hash-slot-cache-ttl`\]</mark> config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.hash-slot-cache-ttl+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".hash-slot-cache-ttl` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".hash-slot-cache-ttl+++[]<br><br>*This property is deprecated since `3.30`: use `quarkus.redis.topology-cache-ttl`.*<br><br>The TTL of the topology cache. A topology cache is used by a clustered Redis client and a sentinel Redis client to prevent constantly sending topology discovery commands (`CLUSTER SLOTS` or `SENTINEL ...`).<br><br>This setting is only meaningful in case of a clustered Redis client and a sentinel Redis client and has no effect otherwise.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_HASH_SLOT_CACHE_TTL+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `1S` |

| [lock] <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-devservices-image-name"></a> [`quarkus.redis.devservices.image-name`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-devservices-image-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.devservices.image-name+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".devservices.image-name` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".devservices.image-name+++[]<br><br>The container image name to use, for container based DevServices providers. If you want to use Redis Stack modules (bloom, graph, search...), use: `redis/redis-stack:latest`.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_DEVSERVICES_IMAGE_NAME+++[] | string | `docker.io/library/redis:7` |
| [lock] <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-devservices-port"></a> [`quarkus.redis.devservices.port`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-devservices-port) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.devservices.port+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".devservices.port` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".devservices.port+++[]<br><br>Optional fixed port the dev service will listen to.<br><br>If not defined, the port will be chosen randomly.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_DEVSERVICES_PORT+++[] | int |  |
| [lock] <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-devservices-shared"></a> [`quarkus.redis.devservices.shared`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-devservices-shared) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.devservices.shared+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".devservices.shared` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".devservices.shared+++[]<br><br>Indicates if the Redis server managed by Quarkus Dev Services is shared. When shared, Quarkus looks for running containers using label-based service discovery. If a matching container is found, it is used, and so a second one is not started. Otherwise, Dev Services for Redis starts a new container.<br><br>The discovery uses the `quarkus-dev-service-redis` label. The value is configured using the `service-name` property.<br><br>Container sharing is only used in dev mode.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_DEVSERVICES_SHARED+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| [lock] <a id="quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-devservices-service-name"></a> [`quarkus.redis.devservices.service-name`](#quarkus-redis-client_quarkus-redis-devservices-service-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis.devservices.service-name+++[]<br><br>`quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".devservices.service-name` config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.redis."redis-client-name".devservices.service-name+++[]<br><br>The value of the `quarkus-dev-service-redis` label attached to the started container. This property is used when `shared` is set to `true`. In this case, before starting a container, Dev Services for Redis looks for a container with the `quarkus-dev-service-redis` label set to the configured value. If found, it will use this container instead of starting a new one. Otherwise, it starts a new container with the `quarkus-dev-service-redis` label set to the specified value.<br><br>This property is used when you need multiple shared Redis servers.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REDIS_DEVSERVICES_SERVICE_NAME+++[] | string | `redis` |

| <a id="quarkus-rest-client-config_quarkus-rest-client-client-logging-scope"></a> [`quarkus.rest-client."client".logging.scope`](#quarkus-rest-client-config_quarkus-rest-client-client-logging-scope) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.rest-client."client".logging.scope+++[]<br><br>Scope of logging for the client.<br><br>> [!WARNING]<br>> beware of logging sensitive data The possible values are:<br><br>\<br> \* `request-response` - enables logging request and responses, including redirect responses \* `all` - enables logging requests and responses and lower-level logging \* `none` - no additional logging<br><br>This property is not applicable to the Quarkus RESTEasy client (provided by the quarkus-resteasy-client dependency).<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_REST_CLIENT__CLIENT__LOGGING_SCOPE+++[] | string |  |

The origin is basically protocol, host and port. If you are calling WebAuthn API while your application is located at `https://example.com/login`, then origin will be `https://example.com`. Please note that WebAuthn API will not work on pages loaded over HTTP, unless it is localhost, which is considered secure context. If unspecified, this defaults to whatever URI this application is deployed on. This allows more than one value if you want to allow multiple origins. Authenticators can interact with the user web browser through several transports. Applications may want to restrict the transport protocols for extra security hardening reasons. By default, all transports should be allowed. If your application is to be used by mobile phone users, you may want to restrict only the `INTERNAL` authenticator to be allowed. Permitted values are:<br><br>\* `USB` - USB connected authenticators (e.g.: Yubikey's) \* `NFC` - NFC connected authenticators (e.g.: Yubikey's) \* `BLE` - Bluetooth LE connected authenticators \* `INTERNAL` - Hardware security chips (e.g.: Intel TPM2.0)<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_TRANSPORTS+++[] | list of `usb`, `nfc`, `ble`, `hybrid`, `internal` | `USB`, `NFC`, `BLE`, `INTERNAL` |

Only useful for attestations different from `Attestation.NONE`.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_LOAD_METADATA+++[] | boolean | `false` |
| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-resident-key"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.resident-key`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-resident-key) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.resident-key+++[]<br><br>Resident key required. A resident (private) key, is a key that cannot leave your authenticator device, this means that you cannot reuse the authenticator to log into a second computer.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_RESIDENT_KEY+++[] | `discouraged`, `preferred`, `required` | `REQUIRED` |
| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-user-verification"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.user-verification`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-user-verification) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.user-verification+++[]<br><br>User Verification requirements. Webauthn applications may choose `REQUIRED` verification to assert that the user is present during the authentication ceremonies, but in some cases, applications may want to reduce the interactions with the user, i.e.: prevent the use of pop-ups. Valid values are:<br><br>\* `REQUIRED` - User must always interact with the browser \* `PREFERRED` - User should always interact with the browser \* `DISCOURAGED` - User should avoid interact with the browser<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_USER_VERIFICATION+++[] | `required`, `preferred`, `discouraged` | `REQUIRED` |
| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-user-presence-required"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.user-presence-required`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-user-presence-required) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.user-presence-required+++[]<br><br>User presence requirements.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_USER_PRESENCE_REQUIRED+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-timeout"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.timeout`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-timeout) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.timeout+++[]<br><br>Non-negative User Verification timeout. Authentication must occur within the timeout, this will prevent the user browser from being blocked with a pop-up required user verification, and the whole ceremony must be completed within the timeout period. After the timeout, any previously issued challenge is automatically invalidated.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_TIMEOUT+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `5m` |
| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-attestation"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.attestation`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-attestation) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.attestation+++[]<br><br>Device Attestation Preference. During registration, applications may want to attest the device. Attestation is a cryptographic verification of the authenticator hardware. Attestation implies that the privacy of the users may be exposed and browsers might override the desired configuration on the user's behalf. Valid values are:<br><br>\* `NONE` - no attestation data is sent with registration \* `INDIRECT` - attestation data is sent with registration, yielding anonymized data by a trusted CA \* `DIRECT` - attestation data is sent with registration \* `ENTERPRISE` - no attestation data is sent with registration. The device AAGUID is returned unaltered.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_ATTESTATION+++[] | `none`, `indirect`, `direct`, `enterprise` | `NONE` |
| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-public-key-credential-parameters"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.public-key-credential-parameters`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-public-key-credential-parameters) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.public-key-credential-parameters+++[]<br><br>Allowed Public Key Credential algorithms by preference order. Webauthn mandates that all authenticators must support at least the following 2 algorithms: `ES256` and `RS256`. Applications may require stronger keys and algorithms, for example: `ES512` or `EdDSA`. Note that the use of stronger algorithms, e.g.: `EdDSA` may require Java 15 or a cryptographic `JCE` provider that implements the algorithms. See <https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-1/++#++dictdef-publickeycredentialparameters><br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_PUBLIC_KEY_CREDENTIAL_PARAMETERS+++[] | list of `es256`, `es384`, `es512`, `ps256`, `ps384`, `ps512`, `es256k`, `rs256`, `rs384`, `rs512`, `rs1`, `ed-dsa` | `ES256`, `RS256` |
| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-challenge-length"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.challenge-length`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-challenge-length) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.challenge-length+++[]<br><br>Length of the challenges exchanged between the application and the browser. Challenges must be at least 32 bytes.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_CHALLENGE_LENGTH+++[] | int | `64` |
| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-login-page"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.login-page`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-login-page) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.login-page+++[]<br><br>The login page<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_LOGIN_PAGE+++[] | string | `/login.html` |
| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-session-timeout"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.session-timeout`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-session-timeout) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.session-timeout+++[]<br><br>The inactivity (idle) timeout When inactivity timeout is reached, cookie is not renewed and a new login is enforced.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_SESSION_TIMEOUT+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `30M` |
| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-new-cookie-interval"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.new-cookie-interval`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-new-cookie-interval) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.new-cookie-interval+++[]<br><br>How old a cookie can get before it will be replaced with a new cookie with an updated timeout, also referred to as "renewal-timeout". Note that smaller values will result in slightly more server load (as new encrypted cookies will be generated more often); however, larger values affect the inactivity timeout because the timeout is set when a cookie is generated. For example if this is set to 10 minutes, and the inactivity timeout is 30m, if a user's last request is when the cookie is 9m old then the actual timeout will happen 21m after the last request because the timeout is only refreshed when a new cookie is generated. That is, no timeout is tracked on the server side; the timestamp is encoded and encrypted in the cookie itself, and it is decrypted and parsed with each request.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_NEW_COOKIE_INTERVAL+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `1M` |

| <a id="quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-cookie-same-site"></a> [`quarkus.webauthn.cookie-same-site`](#quarkus-security-webauthn_quarkus-webauthn-cookie-same-site) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.webauthn.cookie-same-site+++[]<br><br>SameSite attribute for the session cookie.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_WEBAUTHN_COOKIE_SAME_SITE+++[] | `strict`, `lax`, `none` | `strict` |

| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-store-sni"></a> [`quarkus.tls.key-store.sni`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-store-sni) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.key-store.sni+++[]<br><br>Enables Server Name Indication (SNI).<br><br>Server Name Indication (SNI) is a TLS extension that allows a client to specify the hostname it is attempting to connect to during the TLS handshake. This enables a server to present different SSL certificates for multiple domains on a single IP address, facilitating secure communication for virtual hosting scenarios.<br><br>With this setting enabled, the client indicate the server name during the TLS handshake, allowing the server to select the right certificate.<br><br>When configuring the keystore with PEM files, multiple CRT/Key must be given. When configuring the keystore with a JKS or a P12 file, it selects one alias based on the SNI hostname. In this case, all the keystore password and alias password must be the same (configured with the `password` and `alias-password` properties. Do not set the `alias` property.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_KEY_STORE_SNI+++[] | boolean | `false` |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-store-credentials-provider-name"></a> [`quarkus.tls.key-store.credentials-provider.name`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-store-credentials-provider-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.key-store.credentials-provider.name+++[]<br><br>The name of the "credential" bucket (map key -> passwords) to retrieve from the `io.quarkus.credentials.CredentialsProvider`. If not set, the credential provider will not be used.<br><br>A credential provider offers a way to retrieve the key store password as well as alias password. Note that the credential provider is only used if the passwords are not set in the configuration.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_KEY_STORE_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER_NAME+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-store-credentials-provider-bean-name"></a> [`quarkus.tls.key-store.credentials-provider.bean-name`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-store-credentials-provider-bean-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.key-store.credentials-provider.bean-name+++[]<br><br>The name of the bean providing the credential provider.<br><br>The name is used to select the credential provider to use. The credential provider must be exposed as a CDI bean and with the `@Named` annotation set to the configured name to be selected.<br><br>If not set, the default credential provider is used.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_KEY_STORE_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER_BEAN_NAME+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-store-credentials-provider-password-key"></a> [`quarkus.tls.key-store.credentials-provider.password-key`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-store-credentials-provider-password-key) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.key-store.credentials-provider.password-key+++[]<br><br>The key used to retrieve the key store password.<br><br>If the selected credential provider does not support the key, the password is not retrieved. Otherwise, the retrieved value is used to open the key store.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_KEY_STORE_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER_PASSWORD_KEY+++[] | string | `password` |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-store-credentials-provider-alias-password-key"></a> [`quarkus.tls.key-store.credentials-provider.alias-password-key`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-store-credentials-provider-alias-password-key) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.key-store.credentials-provider.alias-password-key+++[]<br><br>The key used to retrieve the key store alias password.<br><br>If the selected credential provider does not contain the key, the alias password is not retrieved. Otherwise, the retrieved value is used to access the alias `private key` from the key store.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_KEY_STORE_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER_ALIAS_PASSWORD_KEY+++[] | string | `alias-password` |

| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-trust-store-credentials-provider-name"></a> [`quarkus.tls.trust-store.credentials-provider.name`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-trust-store-credentials-provider-name) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.trust-store.credentials-provider.name+++[]<br><br>The name of the "credential" bucket (map key -> passwords) to retrieve from the `io.quarkus.credentials.CredentialsProvider`. The credential provider must be exposed as a CDI bean and with the `@Named` annotation set to the configured name to be selected.<br><br>If not set, the default credential provider is used.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_TRUST_STORE_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER_BEAN_NAME+++[] | string |  |

To enable `TLSv1.3` and `TLSv1.2`, set the value to `to "TLSv1.3, TLSv1.2"`.<br><br>Note that setting an empty list, and enabling TLS is invalid. | <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-handshake-timeout"></a> [`quarkus.tls.handshake-timeout`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-handshake-timeout) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.handshake-timeout+++[]<br><br>The timeout for the TLS handshake phase.<br><br>If not set, it defaults to 10 seconds.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT+++[] | [Duration](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html) [[question circle]](#duration-note-anchor-all-config) | `10S` |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-alpn"></a> [`quarkus.tls.alpn`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-alpn) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.alpn+++[]<br><br>Enables the Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN).<br><br>Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation is a TLS extension that allows the client and server during the TLS handshake to negotiate which protocol they will use for communication. ALPN enables more efficient communication by allowing the client to indicate its preferred application protocol to the server before the TLS connection is established. This helps in scenarios such as HTTP/2 where multiple protocols may be available, allowing for faster protocol selection.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_ALPN+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-pqc-enforcement-policy"></a> [`quarkus.tls.pqc-enforcement-policy`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-pqc-enforcement-policy) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.pqc-enforcement-policy+++[]<br><br>Sets the PQC enforcement policy.<br><br>`STRICT`: a connection will be refused unless both the client and the server support a PQC-capable group (`X25519MLKEM768`, `SecP256r1MLKEM768`, `SecP384r1MLKEM1024`). The server requires PQC-capable clients.<br><br>`CLIENT_NEGOTIATED`: the server advertises PQC groups but will not refuse a connection if the client does not support them, allowing fallback to classical key exchange.<br><br>`RELAXED`: no PQC enforcement; standard TLS key exchange negotiation applies.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_PQC_ENFORCEMENT_POLICY+++[] | tooltip:strict[A connection is refused unless both the client and the server negotiate a PQC key exchange (`X25519MLKEM768`,opts=`SecP256r1MLKEM768`,`SecP384r1MLKEM1024`). Clients that do not advertise PQC support are rejected during the TLS handshake.], tooltip:client-negotiated[The server advertises PQC key exchange groups but does not require the client to support them. If the client does not support PQC,opts=the handshake falls back to classical key exchange.], tooltip:relaxed[No PQC enforcement; standard TLS key exchange negotiation applies. The server neither advertises nor requires PQC groups.] | tooltip:relaxed[No PQC enforcement; standard TLS key exchange negotiation applies. The server neither advertises nor requires PQC groups.] |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-exchange-groups"></a> [`quarkus.tls.key-exchange-groups`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-key-exchange-groups) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.key-exchange-groups+++[]<br><br>Sets the ordered list of enabled TLS key exchange groups (supported groups). If not set, the default groups defined by the `SSLEngineOptions` in use are used.<br><br>Example values: `X25519MLKEM768`, `X25519`, `P-256`. When set, these groups take precedence over the engine defaults.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_GROUPS+++[] | list of string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-ssl-engine"></a> [`quarkus.tls.ssl-engine`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-ssl-engine) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.ssl-engine+++[]<br><br>Forces the SSL engine to use.<br><br>When not set, Vert.x selects the engine automatically: if `pqc-enforcement-policy` is `strict` or `client-negotiated`, it prefers the JDK engine (JDK 27{plus}) or falls back to OpenSSL. For `relaxed` policy it uses the JDK engine by default.<br><br>Use `OPENSSL` to force netty-tcnative (requires the native library on the classpath). Use `JDKSSL` to force the standard JDK SSL engine.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_SSL_ENGINE+++[] | tooltip:openssl[Use the OpenSsl Engine,opts=requires netty-tcnative.], tooltip:jdkssl[Use the default JdkSsl Engine.] |  |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-certificate-revocation-list"></a> [`quarkus.tls.certificate-revocation-list`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-certificate-revocation-list) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.certificate-revocation-list+++[]<br><br>Sets the list of revoked certificates (paths to files).<br><br>A Certificate Revocation List (CRL) is a list of digital certificates that have been revoked by the issuing Certificate Authority (CA) before their scheduled expiration date. When a certificate is compromised, no longer needed, or deemed invalid for any reason, the CA adds it to the CRL to inform relying parties not to trust the certificate anymore.<br><br>Two formats are allowed: DER and PKCS++<mark>++7 (also known as P7B). When using the DER format, you must pass DER-encoded CRLs. When using the PKCS++</mark>++7 format, you must pass PKCS++#++7 `SignedData` object, with the only significant field being `crls`.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_CERTIFICATE_REVOCATION_LIST+++[] | list of path |  |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-trust-all"></a> [`quarkus.tls.trust-all`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-trust-all) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.trust-all+++[]<br><br>If set to `true`, the server trusts all certificates.<br><br>This is useful for testing, but should not be used in production.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_TRUST_ALL+++[] | boolean | `false` |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-hostname-verification-algorithm"></a> [`quarkus.tls.hostname-verification-algorithm`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-hostname-verification-algorithm) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.hostname-verification-algorithm+++[]<br><br>The hostname verification algorithm to use in case the server's identity should be checked. Should be `HTTPS` (default), `LDAPS` or `NONE`.<br><br>If set to `NONE`, it does not verify the hostname.<br><br>If not set, the configured extension decides the default algorithm to use. For example, for HTTP, it will be "HTTPS". For TCP, it can depend on the protocol. Nevertheless, it is recommended to set it to "HTTPS" or "LDAPS".<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS_HOSTNAME_VERIFICATION_ALGORITHM+++[] | string |  |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-reload-period"></a> [`quarkus.tls.reload-period`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-reload-period) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls.reload-period+++[]<br><br>When configured, the server will reload the certificates (from the file system for example) and fires a `CertificateUpdatedEvent` if the reload is successful<br><br>This property configures the period to reload the certificates. ALPN enables more efficient communication by allowing the client to indicate its preferred application protocol to the server before the TLS connection is established. This helps in scenarios such as HTTP/2 where multiple protocols may be available, allowing for faster protocol selection.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS__TLS_BUCKET_NAME__ALPN+++[] | boolean | `true` |
| <a id="quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-tls-bucket-name-pqc-enforcement-policy"></a> [`quarkus.tls."tls-bucket-name".pqc-enforcement-policy`](#quarkus-tls-registry_quarkus-tls-tls-bucket-name-pqc-enforcement-policy) config_property_copy_button:+++quarkus.tls."tls-bucket-name".pqc-enforcement-policy+++[]<br><br>Sets the PQC enforcement policy.<br><br>`STRICT`: a connection will be refused unless both the client and the server support a PQC-capable group (`X25519MLKEM768`, `SecP256r1MLKEM768`, `SecP384r1MLKEM1024`). The server requires PQC-capable clients.<br><br>`CLIENT_NEGOTIATED`: the server advertises PQC groups but will not refuse a connection if the client does not support them, allowing fallback to classical key exchange.<br><br>`RELAXED`: no PQC enforcement; standard TLS key exchange negotiation applies.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS__TLS_BUCKET_NAME__PQC_ENFORCEMENT_POLICY+++[] | tooltip:strict[A connection is refused unless both the client and the server negotiate a PQC key exchange (`X25519MLKEM768`,opts=`SecP256r1MLKEM768`,`SecP384r1MLKEM1024`). Clients that do not advertise PQC support are rejected during the TLS handshake.], tooltip:client-negotiated[The server advertises PQC key exchange groups but does not require the client to support them. If the client does not support PQC,opts=the handshake falls back to classical key exchange.], tooltip:relaxed[No PQC enforcement; standard TLS key exchange negotiation applies. The server neither advertises nor requires PQC groups.] | tooltip:relaxed[No PQC enforcement; standard TLS key exchange negotiation applies. The server neither advertises nor requires PQC groups.] |

If not set, the default groups defined by the `SSLEngineOptions` in use are used.<br><br>Example values: `X25519MLKEM768`, `X25519`, `P-256`. When set, these groups take precedence over the engine defaults.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS__TLS_BUCKET_NAME__KEY_EXCHANGE_GROUPS+++[] | list of string |  |

Use `JDKSSL` to force the standard JDK SSL engine.<br><br>Environment variable: env_var_with_copy_button:+++QUARKUS_TLS__TLS_BUCKET_NAME__SSL_ENGINE+++[] | tooltip:openssl[Use the OpenSsl Engine,opts=requires netty-tcnative.], tooltip:jdkssl[Use the default JdkSsl Engine.] |  |

When a certificate is compromised, no longer needed, or deemed invalid for any reason, the CA adds it to the CRL to inform relying parties not to trust the certificate anymore.<br><br>Two formats are allowed: DER and PKCS++<mark>++7 (also known as P7B). <a id="duration-note-anchor-all-config"></a>

> [!NOTE]
> **About the Duration format**
>
> To write duration values, use the standard `java.time.Duration` format. See the [Duration#parse() Java API documentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Duration.html#parse(java.lang.CharSequence)) for more information.
>
> You can also use a simplified format, starting with a number:
>
> - If the value is only a number, it represents time in seconds.
> - If the value is a number followed by `ms`, it represents time in milliseconds.
>
> In other cases, the simplified format is translated to the `java.time.Duration` format for parsing:
>
> - If the value is a number followed by `h`, `m`, or `s`, it is prefixed with `PT`.
> - If the value is a number followed by `d`, it is prefixed with `P`.

<a id="memory-size-note-anchor-all-config"></a>

> [!NOTE]
> **About the MemorySize format**
>
> A size configuration option recognizes strings in this format (shown as a regular expression): `[0-9]+[KkMmGgTtPpEeZzYy]?`.
>
> If no suffix is given, assume bytes.
